nodes.label: impeccable (frontend design skill)
nodes.summary: A 24-command frontend design skill that designs, evaluates, refines, enhances and fixes production UI. Routing: no argument renders the command menu; a matching first word loads that command's reference; anything else is a freeform design invocation under the shared laws.

nodes.label: shape: design brief before code
nodes.summary: Discovery interview (2-3 questions per round, at least one real user-answer round) plus optional visual probes, synthesized into a 10-section design brief that must be explicitly confirmed. Writes no code.

nodes.label: craft: shape-then-build end to end
nodes.summary: Seven-step build loop: shape, load references, land visual direction, extract assets, build to production quality, browser-iterate, present. Runs shape internally and cannot build until the build gate passes.

nodes.label: Teach a topic over multiple sessions
nodes.summary: Turns the working directory into a stateful teaching workspace producing self-contained HTML lessons, reference sheets, and a growing record of what the learner knows.

nodes.label: document: generate DESIGN.md from code
nodes.summary: Scans CSS custom properties, Tailwind config, token files and components to auto-extract a design system, then asks for qualitative language and writes DESIGN.md (Stitch six-section format) plus a DESIGN.json sidecar. Seed mode covers pre-implementation projects.

nodes.label: extract: consolidate reusable patterns
nodes.summary: Finds patterns used 3+ times with the same intent, plans extraction, builds enriched reusable components/tokens, migrates existing uses, and documents them. Refuses premature abstraction.

nodes.label: critique: UX design review with scoring
nodes.summary: Runs two isolated assessments (LLM design review + automated detector), synthesizes a combined report with heuristic scores, anti-pattern verdict, priority issues, persona red flags, then asks targeted questions and emits a ranked command plan.

nodes.label: audit: technical quality checks
nodes.summary: Code-level diagnostic across accessibility, performance, theming, responsive design and anti-patterns, each scored 0-4 for a /20 health score. Documents issues; does not fix them.

nodes.label: polish: final pass before shipping
nodes.summary: Meticulous last pass over alignment, IA/flow shape, typography, color, states, micro-interactions, copy, icons, forms, edge cases, responsiveness, performance and code hygiene. Must not run before the work is functionally complete.

nodes.label: bolder: amplify safe or bland design
nodes.summary: Increases visual impact through typographic, color, spatial, effect, motion and compositional amplification. In the product register it amplifies clarity and hierarchy rather than drama.

nodes.label: quieter: tone down overstimulating design
nodes.summary: Reduces saturation, visual weight, decoration and motion while preserving character and hierarchy. Explicitly not a path to grayscale or genericness.

nodes.label: distill: strip to essence
nodes.summary: Removes complexity across IA, visuals, layout, interaction, content and code so one primary goal and one primary action remain. Simplicity means removing obstacles, not features.

nodes.label: harden: production resilience
nodes.summary: Strengthens against extreme inputs, error scenarios, i18n, edge cases, validation, accessibility resilience and slow connections. Designs that only work with perfect data are not production ready.

nodes.label: onboard: first-run flows and activation
nodes.summary: Designs welcome flows, empty states, contextual tooltips, tours and tutorials aimed at the shortest path to the aha moment, with skip paths and dismissal memory.

nodes.label: animate: purposeful motion
nodes.summary: Adds entrance choreography, micro-interactions, state transitions, navigation motion and delight moments with a named hero moment and explicit duration/easing discipline.

nodes.label: colorize: strategic color introduction
nodes.summary: Introduces semantic color, accent application, tinted surfaces, data-viz encoding and borders into monochromatic UIs, dosed by the chosen color strategy.

nodes.label: typeset: typography hierarchy and fonts
nodes.summary: Assesses generic or muddy type and rebuilds font selection, scale, weight roles, measure and OpenType detail. Register decides fluid clamp scales versus fixed rem scales.

nodes.label: layout: spacing, rhythm and hierarchy
nodes.summary: Fixes arbitrary spacing, weak structure, monotonous card grids and flat hierarchy by establishing a spacing system, rhythm, the right layout tool, and semantic elevation.

nodes.label: delight: personality and memorable moments
nodes.summary: Adds micro-interactions, copy personality, illustrations, sound, easter eggs and celebration moments, sized to the register and never blocking the task.

nodes.label: overdrive: push past conventional limits
nodes.summary: Uses the full browser platform (View Transitions, scroll-driven animation, WebGL/WebGPU, virtual scrolling, Workers, WASM) to make an interface feel extraordinary. Must propose 2-3 directions and get a pick before building.

nodes.label: clarify: UX copy, labels and errors
nodes.summary: Rewrites unclear interface text across errors, labels, CTAs, help text, empty states, success, loading, confirmations and navigation toward specific, active, human, consistent copy.

nodes.label: adapt: retarget across devices and contexts
nodes.summary: Rethinks the experience for a new context (mobile, tablet, desktop, print, email) rather than scaling it, changing layout, interaction, content and navigation strategy per target.

nodes.label: optimize: diagnose and fix UI performance
nodes.summary: Measures Core Web Vitals and bottlenecks, then fixes loading, rendering, animation, framework and network performance. Measure before and after; never optimize blind.

nodes.label: live: in-browser variant mode
nodes.summary: Boot a helper server, inject a picker, and run a poll loop where the user selects an element and the agent generates three hot-swapped HTML+CSS variants with tunable parameters, then accepts one into true source.

nodes.label: the AI slop test
nodes.summary: If someone could look at the interface and say 'AI made that' without doubt, it has failed. Invoked as the pass/fail gate across critique, audit, craft, bolder and both register references.

nodes.label: category-reflex check (two altitudes)
nodes.summary: First-order: if theme and palette are guessable from the category alone it is the training-data reflex. Second-order: if the aesthetic family is guessable from category-plus-anti-references it is the trap one tier deeper. Rework until neither is obvious.

nodes.label: reflex-reject font and aesthetic-lane lists
nodes.summary: Named ban lists of training-data default typefaces (Fraunces, Playfair, Inter, Space Grotesk, DM Sans, Instrument Serif and kin) and saturated aesthetic families (editorial-typographic). Applies to greenfield choices and departure-mode variants, never to an already-committed identity.

nodes.label: register: brand vs product
nodes.summary: Every design task is brand (design IS the product) or product (design SERVES the product). Identified before designing from the task cue, the surface in focus, or PRODUCT.md's register field; the matching reference is loaded and the shared laws apply to both.

nodes.label: color strategy commitment axis
nodes.summary: Four steps of commitment: Restrained (tinted neutrals plus one accent under 10%), Committed (one saturated color across 30-60%), Full palette (3-4 named roles), Drenched (the surface IS the color). Product defaults to Restrained; brand has permission for the rest.

nodes.label: OKLCH as the color space
nodes.summary: Use OKLCH (or LCH) instead of HSL because it is perceptually uniform; hold chroma and hue while varying lightness, and reduce chroma near the extremes because high chroma there looks garish.

nodes.label: tinted neutrals, never pure black or white
nodes.summary: Pure gray and #000/#fff are banned. Every neutral carries 0.005-0.015 chroma hued toward this project's brand color, creating subconscious cohesion without reading as tinted.

nodes.label: never gray text on colored backgrounds
nodes.summary: Gray on color reads washed out and dead. Use a darker shade of the background color or transparency instead.

nodes.label: theme via a physical scene sentence
nodes.summary: Dark versus light is never a default. Write one sentence of physical context (who, where, ambient light, mood) concrete enough that it forces the answer; run the sentence, not the category.

nodes.label: the absolute bans (match and refuse)
nodes.summary: Side-stripe borders over 1px, gradient text via background-clip, decorative glassmorphism, the hero-metric template, identical card grids, and modal-as-first-thought. If about to write one, rewrite the element with different structure.

nodes.label: copy earns its place, no em dashes
nodes.summary: Every word must earn its place, with no restated headings or intros that repeat the title, and no em dashes or double hyphens anywhere in interface copy.

nodes.label: cards are the lazy answer
nodes.summary: Cards are only correct when they are truly the best affordance; nested cards are always wrong. Spacing and alignment create grouping naturally, and not everything needs a container.

nodes.label: non-optional setup gate (preflight)
nodes.summary: Context, product, command-reference, craft-shape, and image gates must all pass before any project file is edited. Codex-style agents state an IMPECCABLE_PREFLIGHT line naming each gate's state before mutating.

nodes.label: PRODUCT.md (strategic context)
nodes.summary: Required project-root file carrying register, users, product purpose, brand personality, anti-references, design principles and accessibility needs. Every other command reads it before working; if missing or placeholder, teach runs as a blocker.

nodes.label: DESIGN.md (visual system spec)
nodes.summary: Optional but strongly recommended visual spec in the Google Stitch format: YAML token frontmatter plus exactly six fixed-order sections (Overview, Colors, Typography, Elevation, Components, Do's and Don'ts). Tokens are normative; prose contextualizes.

nodes.label: DESIGN.json sidecar (extensions)
nodes.summary: Companion file carrying what the Stitch frontmatter schema cannot hold: tonal ramps, shadow and motion tokens, breakpoints, self-contained component HTML/CSS snippets, and the narrative (north star, named rules, do's and don'ts).

nodes.label: confirmed design brief
nodes.summary: The ten-section output of shape: feature summary, primary user action, design direction, scope, layout strategy, key states, interaction model, content requirements, recommended references, open questions. Only counts once the user explicitly confirms it.

nodes.label: visual direction probes and north-star mocks
nodes.summary: 2-4 distinct direction probes in shape and 1-3 resolved north-star comps in craft, generated only when the work is net-new, fidelity is mid-fi or above, and the harness has native image generation. Direction artifacts, never implementation assets.

nodes.label: native image generation (capability gate)
nodes.summary: The probe and mock steps are gated on the harness having a built-in image tool. If unavailable, state the skip in one line and proceed; never ask the user to install APIs, shell scripts or one-off tooling for it.

nodes.label: mock fidelity inventory
nodes.summary: Before building, inventory the approved mock's visible ingredients (hero silhouette, signature motifs, nav/CTA treatment, section sequence, image-native content, type/density/color/motion cues) and decide how each is implemented. Missing major ingredients in the live result are P0 defects.

nodes.label: stop and interview rather than infer
nodes.summary: When context cannot be inferred, stop and use the harness's structured question tool (or ask in chat), 2-3 questions per round, waiting for answers. Inferred answers are hypotheses to confirm, never finished facts.

nodes.label: browser-based critique-and-fix iteration
nodes.summary: Open the result in a real browser, inspect screenshots across mobile/tablet/desktop viewports, write a short self-critique, patch, and re-inspect until no material defects remain. Never stop after the first implementation pass.

nodes.label: two isolated assessments
nodes.summary: Critique launches an LLM design review and an automated detection pass that may not see each other's output, each in its own browser tab, delegated to separate sub-agents. The isolation is what makes the combined score honest.

nodes.label: npx impeccable detector (CLI + live overlay)
nodes.summary: A bundled deterministic scanner flagging 25 AI-slop and design-quality patterns, run as `npx impeccable --json [--fast]` over markup files and as an injected overlay served by `npx impeccable live` whose findings are read from the console.

nodes.label: Nielsen's 10 heuristics, scored 0-4
nodes.summary: Each heuristic scored 0-4 for a total out of 40 with published rating bands (36-40 excellent through 0-11 critical). Most real interfaces score 20-32; a 4 must mean genuinely excellent.

nodes.label: P0-P3 issue severity
nodes.summary: Every finding is tagged Blocking, Major, Minor or Polish, with the tiebreaker question: would a user contact support about this? If yes it is at least P1. Recommended actions are ordered by severity.

nodes.label: persona-based red-flag walkthrough
nodes.summary: Walk the primary user action as 2-3 of five archetypes (Alex power user, Jordan first-timer, Sam accessibility-dependent, Riley stress tester, Casey distracted mobile), reporting named element-level failures rather than generic concerns. Project-specific personas derive from Design Context.

nodes.label: findings-to-command action plan
nodes.summary: Both evaluation commands close by mapping each priority issue to a specific impeccable sub-command in priority order, skipping commands that would address zero issues, and ending the chain with polish.

nodes.label: align to the design system, name the drift's root cause
nodes.summary: Discovery of the design system precedes any other polish work. Each deviation is classified as a missing token, a one-off implementation, or a conceptual misalignment, because the fix differs by category and fixing the symptom compounds drift.

nodes.label: extract only at three uses with the same intent
nodes.summary: Only patterns used 3+ times with the same intent are worth extracting; premature abstraction is worse than duplication, and two things that look similar but serve different purposes stay separate.

nodes.label: the eight interactive states
nodes.summary: Every interactive element needs default, hover, focus, active, disabled, loading, error and success designed. The common miss is designing hover without focus; keyboard users never see hover.

nodes.label: focus rings via :focus-visible
nodes.summary: Never outline:none without a replacement. Show a 2-3px high-contrast offset ring on :focus-visible so keyboard users get the indicator and pointer users do not.

nodes.label: realistic state coverage (empty, loading, error, edge)
nodes.summary: Default, hover, focus, active, disabled, loading, error, success, empty, overflow, long and short text, and first-run states are the definition of done. Each must feel intentional, not like an afterthought.

nodes.label: empty states are onboarding opportunities
nodes.summary: An empty state must say what will appear, why it matters, how to start, carry visual interest, and offer contextual help. Blank space and 'No items' are wasted teaching moments.

nodes.label: Progressive disclosure loading
nodes.summary: Three-level loading: metadata (~100 words, always in context), SKILL.md body (<5k words, loaded on trigger), bundled references and scripts (loaded or executed only when needed). Keeps SKILL.md under ~500 lines by pushing variant detail into references/.

nodes.label: the four-item working memory rule
nodes.summary: Humans hold at most about four items in working memory. At any decision point count the options: 4 or fewer is manageable, 5-7 pushes the boundary, 8 or more means users skip, misclick or abandon.

nodes.label: eight-item cognitive load checklist
nodes.summary: Single focus, chunking, grouping, visual hierarchy, one thing at a time, minimal choices, working memory, progressive disclosure. 0-1 failures is low load, 2-3 moderate, 4 or more critical.

nodes.label: the squint test
nodes.summary: Blur the view (or blur a screenshot) and check whether the most important element, the second most important, and the groupings are still identifiable. If everything reads the same weight, hierarchy is broken.

nodes.label: hierarchy through 2-3 dimensions at once
nodes.summary: Combine size, weight, color, position and space rather than relying on size alone; the best hierarchy uses two or three dimensions together, and space alone is often enough.

nodes.label: a consistent spacing scale with varied rhythm
nodes.summary: Spacing values must come from a defined 4pt-based scale named semantically by relationship, applied with gap rather than margins, and deliberately varied: tight groupings against generous separations. Same padding everywhere is monotony.

nodes.label: container queries for components
nodes.summary: Viewport queries belong to page layout; container queries let the same component stay compact in a sidebar and expand in main content without viewport hacks.

nodes.label: semantic z-index and elevation scales
nodes.summary: Build a named stacking scale (dropdown, sticky, modal-backdrop, modal, toast, tooltip) and a consistent shadow scale instead of arbitrary 999/9999 values. Shadows should be subtle enough that seeing them clearly means they are too strong.

nodes.label: modular type scale with real contrast
nodes.summary: Fewer sizes with more contrast: about five roles on a committed ratio. Brand uses fluid clamp() at 1.25 or higher; product uses a fixed rem scale at 1.125-1.2. Flat scales read as uncommitted and muddy the hierarchy.

nodes.label: cap the measure at 45-75ch
nodes.summary: Body line length is capped with ch units around 65-75 characters, with line-height scaling inversely to line length. Data and compact UI can run denser.

nodes.label: light-on-dark text needs three-axis compensation
nodes.summary: Light type on dark reads lighter: bump line-height 0.05-0.1, add 0.01-0.02em letter-spacing, and optionally step body weight up one notch. Fix all three axes, not just one.

nodes.label: web font loading without layout shift
nodes.summary: font-display swap or optional, metric-matched fallbacks via size-adjust and ascent/descent overrides, preload only the critical weight, and prefer a variable font at three or more weights.

nodes.label: the 100/300/500 duration ladder
nodes.summary: 100-150ms for instant feedback, 200-300ms for state changes, 300-500ms for layout changes, 500-800ms for entrances, with exits at about 75% of the enter duration and nothing over 500ms for feedback.

nodes.label: exponential ease-out, never bounce or elastic
nodes.summary: Use ease-out-quart / quint / expo for natural deceleration. Bounce and elastic curves feel dated and draw attention to the animation instead of the content.

nodes.label: do not casually animate layout properties
nodes.summary: Avoid animating width, height, top, left and margins; use transform, FLIP or grid-template-rows instead, and keep expensive blur/filter/shadow areas bounded and verified smooth in-browser.

nodes.label: premium motion materials beyond transform/opacity
nodes.summary: Blur, backdrop-filter, masks, clip paths, shadow bloom, SVG filters and gradient movement are legitimate motion materials when they make the interaction feel more premium and stay smooth on target viewports.

nodes.label: respect prefers-reduced-motion
nodes.summary: A hard accessibility requirement, not a suggestion: provide a crossfade or static alternative while preserving functional animation like progress and focus indicators. Vestibular disorders affect roughly 35% of adults over 40.

nodes.label: perceived performance over measured speed
nodes.summary: What matters is how fast it feels: under 80ms reads as instant, passive waiting feels longer than active engagement, and preemptive starts, progressive completion and optimistic UI shift the balance. Too-fast results can even reduce perceived value.

nodes.label: Core Web Vitals as the performance target
nodes.summary: LCP under 2.5s, INP under 200ms and CLS under 0.1, each with named fixes, measured before and after on real devices and throttled networks rather than desktop Chrome on fast wifi.

nodes.label: WCAG contrast requirements
nodes.summary: 4.5:1 for body text, 3:1 for large text and UI components, with 7:1 as the AAA target. Placeholder text still needs 4.5:1, and light gray on white is the most common failure.

nodes.label: never convey meaning by color alone
nodes.summary: Color must be paired with icons, labels or patterns; roughly 8% of men cannot distinguish red from green, and screen-reader users get nothing from a color cue.

nodes.label: 44x44 minimum touch targets
nodes.summary: Interactive elements need at least a 44x44 tap area, expanded with padding or a pseudo-element when the visual size is smaller, with adequate spacing between neighbors.

nodes.label: detect input method, not just screen size
nodes.summary: Screen width does not imply pointer type. Use pointer: fine/coarse and hover: hover/none queries, and never make functionality depend on hover.

nodes.label: content-driven, mobile-first breakpoints
nodes.summary: Start with mobile base styles and layer complexity with min-width queries; let the content decide where it breaks rather than chasing device sizes, and use clamp() for fluid values without breakpoints.

nodes.label: budget for translation expansion and RTL
nodes.summary: German runs about 30% longer and Finnish 30-40%; budget 30-40% extra space, avoid fixed widths on text containers, use logical CSS properties for RTL, and use the Intl API for dates, numbers and plurals.

nodes.label: specific verb-plus-object labels
nodes.summary: Never OK, Submit or Yes/No. Say what will happen ('Save changes', 'Create account', 'Delete 5 items'), and name the destruction for destructive actions.

nodes.label: the error message formula
nodes.summary: Every error answers what happened, why, and how to fix it, in plain language, near the source, without blaming the user and without humor.

nodes.label: one term, used everywhere
nodes.summary: Pick one word per concept (Delete not Remove/Trash; Settings not Preferences/Options) and enforce it with a glossary. Variety in terminology creates confusion, and the same noun must mean the same thing across screens.

nodes.label: undo beats confirmation
nodes.summary: Users click through confirmations mindlessly. Remove from the UI immediately and offer an undo toast; reserve confirmation for truly irreversible, high-cost or batch actions.

nodes.label: overlay positioning without clipping
nodes.summary: position:absolute inside overflow:hidden is the most common generated-code dropdown bug. Escape it with the Popover API top layer, CSS anchor positioning, a portal, or position:fixed with boundary checks.

nodes.label: progressive enhancement is non-negotiable
nodes.summary: Every advanced technique degrades gracefully via @supports or feature detection, and the experience without the enhancement must still be good. Bleeding-edge APIs always need a functional fallback.

nodes.label: propose directions before building
nodes.summary: For the highest-misfire work, think through 2-3 directions with described look and feel and trade-offs, and get the user's pick before writing code. Skipping it risks building something that has to be thrown away.

nodes.label: ship real imagery when the brief implies it
nodes.summary: For restaurants, hotels, magazines, travel, food, fashion and similar surfaces, zero images is a bug, not restraint. Use stock (Unsplash) searched for the brand's physical object, one decisive photo over five mediocre ones, with alt text in voice.

nodes.label: the font selection procedure
nodes.summary: Write three concrete brand-voice words, list the three reflex fonts and reject any on the ban list, browse a real catalog hunting the brand as a physical object, then cross-check: if the pick matches the original reflex, start over.

nodes.label: identity lock (extract before varying)
nodes.summary: In live mode, extract the surface's actual identity from DESIGN.md, CSS custom properties, computed styles and sibling components into one factual sentence before planning. Skipping it is the primary cause of off-brand variants.

nodes.label: default mode vs departure mode
nodes.summary: Variants preserve the existing identity in about 90% of live sessions. Departure mode is triggered only by PRODUCT.md anti-references naming this surface or an explicit user request; when unsure, default, because off-brand variants are the unrecoverable error.

nodes.label: three variants, three different axes
nodes.summary: Each variant commits to a different primary axis (hierarchy, topology, typographic system, color strategy, density, structural decomposition) or, in departure mode, a different concrete aesthetic direction, verified by a family pass and a sentence pass.

nodes.label: live variant parameter budget
nodes.summary: Variants expose 0-4 coarse knobs (range, steps, toggle) declared as a JSON manifest and driving CSS variables or data attributes, budgeted by the element's visual weight: 0 for a leaf, 2 for a medium composition, 2-3 for a hero. Under-shipping knobs is the common freeform failure.

nodes.label: carbonize cleanup after accept
nodes.summary: When an accepted variant is stitched in temporarily, the agent must synchronously move the CSS to the real stylesheet, bake parameter values, unwrap the variant div, and delete the markers and dead @scope rules before polling again.

nodes.label: never persist into generated files
nodes.summary: The wrap and accept helpers refuse to write into generated or untracked files because accepting there is silent data loss; the agent-driven fallback locates the true source (template, component, or data) and persists the accepted variant there.

nodes.label: load-context.mjs / live.mjs context loader
nodes.summary: A Node script that resolves PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md from the project root or fallback directories, migrates legacy .impeccable.md, and returns full JSON that must be consumed whole. It is re-run after teach or document rewrite the files.

nodes.label: Slash command authoring
nodes.summary: Create Claude Code slash commands as markdown files with optional YAML frontmatter, dynamic arguments, file references and inline bash. Treated as a legacy format superseded by the SKILL.md directory layout, but loaded identically.

nodes.label: Write instructions for the agent, not the user
nodes.summary: Command and skill bodies become the agent's instructions when invoked, so they must be directives to Claude about what to do rather than descriptions to a human about what will happen.

nodes.label: YAML frontmatter contract
nodes.summary: Every command and skill declares itself through optional YAML frontmatter: name, description, allowed-tools, model, argument-hint, disable-model-invocation. The description is the discovery and trigger surface.

nodes.label: Least-privilege tool scoping
nodes.summary: allowed-tools should be the most restrictive set that works, using command filters such as Bash(git:*) rather than Bash(*). Safety lives in the tool layer, not in prose.

nodes.label: Dynamic argument substitution
nodes.summary: $ARGUMENTS captures all arguments as one string; $1/$2/$3 capture positional arguments. argument-hint documents the expected shape for autocomplete.

nodes.label: Inline bash context injection
nodes.summary: Backtick-bang syntax executes a shell command at invocation time and splices its output into the prompt, so the agent starts with live repo or environment state rather than asking for it.

nodes.label: @-syntax file reference inclusion
nodes.summary: @path or @$1 pulls a file's contents into the prompt before processing, letting a command operate on named files without a separate Read step.

nodes.label: CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT portable paths
nodes.summary: ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} resolves to the plugin's absolute directory so bundled scripts, templates and config are referenced portably instead of by hardcoded or cwd-relative paths.

nodes.label: Namespaced command organization
nodes.summary: Subdirectories under commands/ create namespaces shown in /help, used once a set exceeds roughly 15 items or a plugin ships 5+ commands, and to avoid name collisions across plugins.

nodes.label: Validate inputs before acting
nodes.summary: Check required arguments, valid enum values, file existence and plugin resource availability early, and report what is missing with corrective guidance rather than proceeding on bad input.

nodes.label: Graceful failure, rollback and checkpoints
nodes.summary: Workflows detect non-zero exits, offer recovery options, roll back to a saved prior state, and log checkpoints so an interrupted run can resume rather than restart.

nodes.label: Persistent workflow state file
nodes.summary: Multi-invocation workflows carry state in a git- or repo-local markdown file (a .local.md state file, a decision map, a pulled manifest) that each step reads, updates and eventually cleans up.

nodes.label: Workflow locking against concurrency
nodes.summary: A lock file blocks a second concurrent run of a stateful workflow and is removed on completion, preventing two agents from corrupting the same shared state.

nodes.label: Command composition and chaining
nodes.summary: Each command does one thing; a meta-command orchestrates a sequence of them, and pipeline commands consume the output of prior steps. Loose coupling and standard interfaces are the enabling rule.

nodes.label: AskUserQuestion decision wizard
nodes.summary: For choices that need explained trade-offs or multi-select, a command calls AskUserQuestion with 2-4 described options rather than relying on positional arguments, and adapts later questions to earlier answers.

nodes.label: One question at a time interviewing
nodes.summary: Clarifying questions are asked singly, multiple-choice where possible, never batched into one overwhelming message. Shared by brainstorming's design flow and wayfinder's grilling tickets.

nodes.label: Grilling interview
nodes.summary: Interview the user relentlessly to walk a decision tree or mine raw material, checkpointing as you go. Used to explore a chosen architecture candidate and to extract writing fragments.

nodes.label: Answer from the codebase before asking
nodes.summary: If a question can be answered by reading the code or the live system, do that instead of spending the user's attention on it. Applies to grilling, triage context gathering and file discovery.

nodes.label: Active domain modeling
nodes.summary: Challenge terms against the glossary, sharpen fuzzy language into canonical terms, stress-test relationships with concrete scenarios, and write CONTEXT.md and ADRs the moment decisions crystallise.

nodes.label: CONTEXT.md ubiquitous-language glossary
nodes.summary: An opinionated glossary of context-specific terms with an _Avoid_ list of rejected synonyms. Devoid of implementation detail; a CONTEXT-MAP.md at the root signals a multi-context repo.

nodes.label: Architectural decision record
nodes.summary: A sequentially numbered file in docs/adr/ recording in one to three sentences what the context was, what was decided, and why. Value is in recording that a decision happened, not in filling sections.

nodes.label: ADR three-test gate
nodes.summary: Only offer an ADR when the decision is hard to reverse, surprising without context, and the result of a real trade-off. If any of the three is missing, skip it.

nodes.label: Create files lazily
nodes.summary: Do not scaffold empty structure. Create CONTEXT.md when the first term resolves, docs/adr/ when the first ADR is needed, a student folder only when a real relationship exists.

nodes.label: Cross-reference stated behavior against code
nodes.summary: When the user asserts how something works, check whether the code agrees and surface the contradiction rather than accepting the claim. Triage applies the same check for redundancy against existing implementations.

nodes.label: Decision map with fog of war
nodes.summary: Turn a loose idea into a compact markdown map of numbered investigation tickets with blocked-by edges, deliberately incomplete beyond the frontier, pushed forward one resolved ticket per session.

nodes.label: Ticket sized to one agent session
nodes.summary: Each decision-map ticket must fit a single ~100K-token session, and the whole map is loaded as context every session, so the map itself must stay compact and link out to assets rather than inlining them.

nodes.label: Offer to skip the heavyweight process
nodes.summary: When grilling surfaces no fog of war, or a decision is easy to reverse, or a change is trivial, explicitly offer to skip the ceremony and implement directly.

nodes.label: Issue and PR triage state machine
nodes.summary: Move issues and external PRs through two category roles (bug, enhancement) and five state roles (needs-triage, needs-info, ready-for-agent, ready-for-human, wontfix). A PR is treated as an issue with attached code.

nodes.label: Agent brief
nodes.summary: A structured comment posted when an issue or PR reaches ready-for-agent: category, summary, current vs desired behavior, key interfaces, testable acceptance criteria and explicit out-of-scope. It is the contract an AFK agent works from.

nodes.label: Durability over precision in specs
nodes.summary: Briefs describe interfaces, types and behavioral contracts, never file paths or line numbers, because the spec may sit unworked for weeks while the codebase moves under it. Behavioral, not procedural.

nodes.label: Testable acceptance criteria with scope bounds
nodes.summary: Every delegated unit of work carries independently verifiable done-criteria plus an explicit out-of-scope list, so the agent knows when it is finished and does not gold-plate adjacent features.

nodes.label: Out-of-scope rejection knowledge base
nodes.summary: One markdown file per rejected concept in .out-of-scope/ recording the durable reasoning plus a Prior requests list, checked by concept similarity during triage so the same request is not re-litigated.

nodes.label: Already-implemented is not a rejection
nodes.summary: Closing something as wontfix because it already exists must not be written to .out-of-scope/; doing so poisons the dedup checks with false rejections. Point to where the feature lives instead.

nodes.label: Verify the claim before grilling or delegating
nodes.summary: Before any grilling or brief-writing, reproduce the reported bug from the reporter's steps or check out the PR and run its tests. A confirmed verification makes a far stronger agent brief; failure to reproduce is a needs-info signal.

nodes.label: Evidence before completion claims
nodes.summary: No completion, passing or fixed claim without fresh verification output in the current message. Identify the proving command, run it in full, read the output and exit code, then claim with the evidence attached.

nodes.label: Verify persisted state, not the local view
nodes.summary: After a write, re-read the authoritative surface to confirm it landed: reload the profile page rather than trusting the modal, reload the plugin then check dev:errors, check the VCS diff rather than the agent's success report.

nodes.label: Rationalization red-flag table
nodes.summary: A named list of the thoughts that precede a discipline breach ("just this once", "should work now", "this is a simple question", "the skill is overkill") paired with the reality that overrides each.

nodes.label: Mandatory skill invocation before acting
nodes.summary: If there is even a 1% chance a skill applies, invoke it before any response or action including clarifying questions and codebase exploration, announce "Using [skill] to [purpose]", and follow it exactly.

nodes.label: Process skills outrank implementation skills
nodes.summary: When several skills apply, process skills set the approach first and implementation skills carry it out. "Let's build X" routes to brainstorming first; "fix this bug" routes to systematic debugging first.

nodes.label: User instructions override skills override defaults
nodes.summary: CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and direct requests take precedence over skills, which override default behavior. Skill workflows are skipped only on explicit human instruction. Subagents dispatched for a specific task ignore the invocation mandate.

nodes.label: Cross-harness tool mapping
nodes.summary: Skills speak in actions (dispatch a subagent, create a todo); per-harness reference files translate those actions into the concrete tools available on Codex, Pi and Antigravity, and say what to do when no equivalent exists.

nodes.label: Subagent dispatch availability
nodes.summary: Parallel-agent and subagent-driven skills need real dispatch primitives: Codex requires multi_agent = true for spawn/wait/close, Antigravity uses invoke_subagent, Pi may have none. Never fabricate Task calls when the capability is absent.

nodes.label: Checklist task tracking
nodes.summary: Multi-step work maintains a live checklist as the source of truth for what remains: a todo per skill checklist item, an Antigravity task artifact, or a repo TODO.md on harnesses without a task tool.

nodes.label: Read-only environment detection before branching
nodes.summary: Before creating worktrees or finishing branches, probe git with read-only commands: a differing git-dir and git-common-dir means an existing linked worktree, an empty branch name means detached HEAD and no push or PR from the sandbox.

nodes.label: Single ingest front door
nodes.summary: One entry point for getting anything into the brain: routes web clips, Gemini transcripts, knowledge sources and bulk exports to their pipeline, so the user never has to know which pipeline a thing belongs to.

nodes.label: Dedupe by content hash before ingesting
nodes.summary: Hash the candidate with shasum -a 256 and compare against filed material of the same size, because a byte-identical copy under a different filename has already been ingested. Also check wiki/log.md for the source name.

nodes.label: Sources are immutable
nodes.summary: raw/ is never modified, moved or deleted; duplicates are flagged for the human to decide. Bulk PII exports are inventoried rather than read wholesale, and government IDs stop the ingest entirely.

nodes.label: Generated mirrors are never hand-edited
nodes.summary: Files that mirror a live backend (*.generated.md, the roster, pulled submissions) are regenerated, never written by hand, and the backend stays the source of truth the local copy reflects.

nodes.label: Prefer the inventory script over hand-derivation
nodes.summary: Run the read-only inventory script to map transcripts to students rather than re-parsing filenames each session; when it gets something wrong, fix the script or the alias file instead of working around it silently.

nodes.label: Pull booking-time student submissions
nodes.summary: Authenticate as admin against the LSAT U backend, list bookings carrying notes or files, and mirror the comments and signed-URL downloads into students/<name>/submissions/. On-demand only, no cron or watcher.

nodes.label: Idempotent pull via manifest
nodes.summary: A per-student .pulled.json records which redemption ids have already been fetched so re-running only pulls what is new, and a --dry-run mode lists without writing.

nodes.label: Morning inbox brief
nodes.summary: One daily pass that sweeps Gmail, classifies every waiting message into a bucket, ranks the queue, drafts each reply in the user's voice and logs it. Exists because 19% of his emails are late-reply apologies.

nodes.label: Draft by default, send only on explicit go-ahead
nodes.summary: Anything a student or prospect reads is drafted and not sent unless pre-approved and explicitly green-lit; the --draft flag is never omitted on a first pass. A batch is drafted whole and approved once, and never sent on an ambiguous 'yes'.

nodes.label: Rank by cost of continued silence
nodes.summary: Order the reply queue by what silence costs rather than arrival time: aging consultations, then blocked active students, then fast-decaying new inquiries, then scheduling. State each item's age in days.

nodes.label: Log every draft to the send ledger
nodes.summary: Each created draft is appended to wiki/send-ledger.md with status 'drafted'; Gmail remains the authority for whether anything was actually sent. Inbound message patterns are logged to the outreach log.

nodes.label: Voice gate for human-facing copy
nodes.summary: Anything a student or prospect will read routes through the saved teaching voice and confirmed vault facts: no em-dashes, no AI-slop vocabulary, no invented credentials, dates or experience.

nodes.label: Stop-before-consequential-action gate
nodes.summary: Irreversible or judgment-bearing actions halt for explicit human authorization: uploads, policy agreement and final submission; creating a student folder; state overrides; and disable-model-invocation on commands that must be typed by a human.

nodes.label: TutorOcean profile fill
nodes.summary: Populate the tutor application and profile from vault-confirmed facts and saved LSAT story copy, verifying each save in the profile view, and stopping before uploads, policy agreement or submission.

nodes.label: Session pickup briefing
nodes.summary: On explicit request only, read the task ledger, hot cache, dashboard, index and latest log entry, follow the resume pointer to any active plan file, then emit a 6-8 line briefing and stop without starting work.

nodes.label: Lazy retrieval to protect the context budget
nodes.summary: Load only what the current step needs: skim the index rather than crawling pages, read only the messages you are about to draft for, never read a PII export wholesale, and let references and examples load on demand.

nodes.label: Carry open questions forward, re-check stale state
nodes.summary: Unresolved questions from a prior handoff are re-surfaced and re-asked rather than silently rolling forward, and any load-bearing claim about a live system is re-verified rather than restated as current.

nodes.label: gws CLI
nodes.summary: The Google Workspace CLI binary that every gws-* skill wraps, with a shared syntax (`gws <service> <resource> <method>`), global flags (--format, --dry-run, --sanitize), pagination flags, and OAuth or service-account auth.

nodes.label: Inspect Schema Before Calling an API Method
nodes.summary: Run the CLI's schema/help subcommand to learn a method's required params, types, and defaults before constructing the call, rather than guessing flags.

nodes.label: Label read-only versus write commands
nodes.summary: Each helper command states plainly whether it mutates anything: standup-report is read-only and never modifies data, file-announce is a write command that sends a Chat message.

nodes.label: Cross-service aggregation into one summary
nodes.summary: Workflow helpers combine two or more services into a single answer: today's calendar agenda plus the open task list as a standup, or a Drive upload followed by a Chat announcement.

nodes.label: Obsidian CLI dependency
nodes.summary: The obsidian binary drives a running Obsidian instance for reading, creating, searching and property editing, plus a plugin dev loop of plugin:reload, dev:errors, dev:screenshot and dev:console.

nodes.label: Obsidian Bases declarative views
nodes.summary: A .base YAML file defines filters, computed formulas, property display names, summaries and one or more table, cards, list or map views, producing database-like queries over vault notes.

nodes.label: YAML quoting and Duration-type pitfalls
nodes.summary: The common Bases breakages: unquoted strings containing YAML special characters, double quotes nested inside double quotes in formulas, referencing an undefined formula, and doing arithmetic on a Duration without first accessing .days.

nodes.label: Snapshot-then-interact browser automation
nodes.summary: Chrome DevTools MCP drives a page by navigating, waiting, taking an accessibility snapshot for element uids, then acting on those uids. Text snapshots are preferred over screenshots for automation.

nodes.label: Higgsfield website and app builder
nodes.summary: Drive the full lifecycle of a React 19 + TanStack Start SSR Cloudflare Worker through the higgsfield website CLI, routed at create time by a required --type of website (standalone) or app (Higgsfield-integrated).

nodes.label: Layered command testing
nodes.summary: Seven escalating levels from frontmatter syntax validation through argument matrices, file references, bash execution and integration, wired into a suite script, a pre-commit hook and CI.

nodes.label: Self-documenting command header
nodes.summary: An HTML comment block in the command file carrying purpose, usage, arguments, examples, requirements, related commands, troubleshooting and changelog, so the docs travel with the artifact.

nodes.label: Versioning, deprecation and migration notes
nodes.summary: Semantic versions with a changelog, breaking changes called out with migration guidance, and deprecation warnings that name the replacement and the removal version before a feature disappears.

nodes.label: Distribution readiness
nodes.summary: Making a command survive unknown environments: platform detection, dependency probing with install guidance, graceful degradation when optional tools are absent, first-run onboarding and a pre-release checklist.

nodes.label: Skill authoring and iterative improvement
nodes.summary: skill-creator's own capability: draft a SKILL.md, run test prompts with and without the skill, review outputs with the user, and rewrite until satisfied. Also packages and ships the finished .skill file.

nodes.label: TDD applied to process documentation
nodes.summary: Skill creation follows RED-GREEN-REFACTOR: run a baseline scenario without the skill, write the minimal skill addressing the observed failures, then close loopholes. The Iron Law is no skill without a failing test first.

nodes.label: Establish a no-guidance baseline first
nodes.summary: Never write guidance without first observing the failure it is meant to prevent. Anthropic's evaluation-driven development and writing-skills' RED phase both mandate measuring the agent without the skill before writing it.

nodes.label: Pressure-scenario subagent testing
nodes.summary: Test a discipline skill by giving a fresh subagent a realistic task combining 3+ pressures (time, sunk cost, authority, exhaustion) and forcing an explicit A/B/C choice, then capturing rationalizations verbatim.

nodes.label: Micro-test wording against a control
nodes.summary: Before full pressure scenarios, verify guidance wording with 5+ fresh-context samples per variant plus a no-guidance control, reading every flagged match manually. Variance across reps is itself a metric of non-binding wording.

nodes.label: Bulletproofing against rationalization
nodes.summary: Close loopholes explicitly, add a foundational 'violating the letter is violating the spirit' principle, build a rationalization table from baseline testing, and publish a red-flags self-check list.

nodes.label: Match guidance form to failure type
nodes.summary: Prohibitions bulletproof discipline failures but measurably backfire on output-shaping failures, where a positive recipe or contract wins. Omissions want a structural REQUIRED slot; conditional behavior wants an observable predicate.

nodes.label: Prohibition backfires on shaping problems
nodes.summary: Under a competing incentive, agents negotiate with 'don't X'. Head-to-head tests showed the prohibition arm produced more unwanted content than the recipe arm and trended worse than the no-guidance control. Nuance and exemption clauses reopen the negotiation.

nodes.label: Persuasion principles for compliance
nodes.summary: Authority, commitment, scarcity, social proof, and unity raise agent compliance (Cialdini 2021; Meincke et al. 2025, 33% to 72%). Liking and reciprocity are avoided because they create sycophancy.

nodes.label: Skill discovery optimization
nodes.summary: Descriptions are the only metadata preloaded, so they must be third-person, start with 'Use when', carry searchable symptoms and keywords, and be discoverable among 100+ skills.

nodes.label: Description that summarizes workflow becomes a shortcut
nodes.summary: When a description summarizes the skill's process, agents follow the description and skip the body. A description mentioning 'code review between tasks' caused one review where the flowchart mandated two.

nodes.label: Set degrees of freedom to task fragility
nodes.summary: High freedom (prose) when many approaches are valid; low freedom (an exact script, no flags) when operations are fragile and a specific sequence must hold. The narrow-bridge vs open-field heuristic.

nodes.label: Validate-then-proceed feedback loop
nodes.summary: Run a validator, fix errors, repeat, and only proceed when it passes. Works with a script validator or a style-guide checklist; the plan-validate-execute variant adds a machine-checkable intermediate plan file.

nodes.label: Subagent-driven plan execution
nodes.summary: Execute an implementation plan by dispatching a fresh implementer subagent per task, a task review after each, and a broad whole-branch review at the end, continuously and without human check-ins between tasks.

nodes.label: Fresh isolated context per delegated task
nodes.summary: A subagent never inherits the session's history; the controller constructs exactly the task, the interfaces it touches, and the global constraints. One real dispatch hit 42k chars of which 99% was pasted history.

nodes.label: Hand artifacts over as files, not pasted text
nodes.summary: Task briefs, implementer reports, and review packages move as uniquely named files whose paths appear in the prompt, so bulk content never enters the controller's context and is not re-read every turn.

nodes.label: Durable progress ledger
nodes.summary: A git-ignored progress.md recording 'Task N: complete (commits base..head, review clean)'. Conversation memory does not survive compaction; controllers that lost their place re-dispatched whole completed sequences.

nodes.label: Post-compaction re-dispatch of completed work
nodes.summary: After autocompaction a controller forgets which tasks it finished and re-runs them. Named the single most expensive failure observed; the ledger plus git log is the recovery map.

nodes.label: Model selection by task complexity
nodes.summary: Use the least powerful model that can do each role, always specified explicitly since an omitted model inherits the session's most expensive one. Turn count beats token price, so mid-tier is the floor for reviewers.

nodes.label: Implementer status contract
nodes.summary: Implementers report exactly DONE, DONE_WITH_CONCERNS, BLOCKED, or NEEDS_CONTEXT, under 15 lines, with detail in a report file. Escalation is always allowed; never force the same model to retry unchanged.

nodes.label: Adversarial verification before shipping
nodes.summary: Nothing ships on the producer's own say-so. A separate reviewer (subagent, a different model, or Claude reading Codex's diff) attacks the artifact, and the producer's stated rationale never downgrades a finding.

nodes.label: Dual-verdict task review (spec + quality)
nodes.summary: One reviewer reads the task's diff once and returns two required verdicts: spec compliance (missing / extra / misunderstood, with a warn tier for what the diff cannot show) and code quality graded Critical / Important / Minor.

nodes.label: Never pre-judge findings for a reviewer
nodes.summary: A dispatch must not tell a reviewer what to ignore or pre-rate a finding's severity. Phrases like 'do not flag' or 'at most Minor' mean the controller is sparing itself a review loop; plan-mandated defects are the human's call.

nodes.label: Treat the producer's report as unverified claims
nodes.summary: The reviewer verifies the implementer's report against the diff rather than accepting it; Claude reads Codex's full diff and runs the proof command itself rather than accepting pasted output.

nodes.label: Relentless one-question-at-a-time interview
nodes.summary: Walk every branch of the design tree, asking one question at a time and waiting for the answer, always offering a recommended answer, and exploring the codebase instead of asking whenever the code can answer.

nodes.label: Grill me (plan interview)
nodes.summary: A relentless interview that sharpens a plan or design before building. In the Codex catalog it is a thin, model-invocation-disabled shim that delegates to a /grilling session.

nodes.label: Checkpoint state to disk, not context
nodes.summary: Long sessions fill context and the agent will eventually misremember, conflate, or drop something, so durable state is written to a file after each increment rather than held in the conversation.

nodes.label: grill-me-codex: two-act plan hardening
nodes.summary: Act 1 grills the user until intent is locked into PLAN.md; Act 2 hands that plan to OpenAI Codex for adversarial read-only review until APPROVED or MAX_ROUNDS. Act 1 is Matt Pocock's grill-me under MIT.

nodes.label: Cross-model adversarial review
nodes.summary: A different model attacks the artifact so there is no echo chamber. Codex returns exactly one VERDICT line (APPROVED or REVISE); Claude stays final arbiter, incorporating good critiques and logging rejected ones.

nodes.label: Bounded iteration with an explicit cap
nodes.summary: Review and fix loops always terminate at MAX_ROUNDS / MAX_FIX_ROUNDS. On deadlock, do not fake convergence: list unresolved points for the human. On spent fix rounds, Claude takes over rather than ping-ponging.

nodes.label: Resume the same Codex thread across rounds
nodes.summary: Capture thread_id from the thread.started JSON line and resume it every later round so the reviewer keeps its prior critiques. A fresh exec re-reads the whole repo and discards everything settled; --last can grab the wrong thread.

nodes.label: Codex CLI as a tool dependency
nodes.summary: codex >= 0.130, authenticated via codex login, with the model left unpinned because gpt-5.x-codex variants 400 on ChatGPT-account auth. The active model is echoed to the user before spending a round.

nodes.label: codex exec hangs without stdin EOF
nodes.summary: codex exec reads stdin in addition to the prompt argument, so under a non-TTY driver it blocks forever at ~0% CPU. The fix is < /dev/null (or feeding the prompt file on stdin) plus a 10-minute timeout ceiling.

nodes.label: Resume silently inherits the wrong sandbox
nodes.summary: codex exec resume rejects -s, so without an explicit sandbox_mode override it inherits config.toml and a read-only reviewer could write files; symmetrically a builder resume without the long bypass flag cannot write.

nodes.label: codex-build: Codex types, Claude verifies
nodes.summary: The role-flip of the review loop: Codex implements a frozen spec with full write access in a --yolo sandbox while Claude writes the spec, reads the whole diff like a contributor PR, and runs the proof.

nodes.label: PLAN.md frozen spec
nodes.summary: A locked plan with goal, numbered approach, key decisions and tradeoffs, risks, and out-of-scope bounds. It is the output of the grill and the required input to delegated implementation.

nodes.label: PLAN-REVIEW-LOG.md append-only transcript
nodes.summary: The deliverable that keeps the whole argument: each round's critique, Claude's response with what was rejected and why, and the Act 3 build record, so one file tells the grilled-reviewed-built-verified story.

nodes.label: Never delegate a build without a spec
nodes.summary: Building from a rough idea is designing by delegation and fails. If writing the spec forces decisions, that is a grill, and design stays with Claude. Also excluded: ~<20-line edits where delegation overhead loses.

nodes.label: Clean working tree before delegated writes
nodes.summary: git status must be clean before launching a write-access agent, non-negotiable, because a dirty tree means its diff cannot be isolated or cleanly reverted.

nodes.label: Human sign-off before any code
nodes.summary: No code is written during either act. After convergence the human picks whether Codex builds it, Claude builds it, or work stops. The same gate appears in the CLAUDE.md improver, which never writes until the report is approved.

nodes.label: Inspect, recommend, wait for approval, then execute
nodes.summary: The recurring shape for anything destructive: inspect reality, summarize it, recommend options, wait for approval, execute only what was approved, report exact changes.

nodes.label: prompt-architect-refiner: prompt engineering
nodes.summary: Turn rough instructions into execution-ready prompts using a silent 10-part framework (role, goal, context, inputs, constraints, workflow, output, quality bar, verification, stopping rule), with per-tool modes.

nodes.label: Add a stopping rule to any mutating prompt
nodes.summary: Prompts that could modify files, code, databases, or external accounts get an explicit stopping rule and approval checkpoint; destructive permissions without a checkpoint are an anti-pattern to strip out.

nodes.label: Inspect before claiming
nodes.summary: Never let an agent assert it inspected something it did not. Code prompts require repo inspection before claims; the wiki query cites pages; the QA skill explores the codebase before filing.

nodes.label: setup-matt-pocock-skills: per-repo skill config
nodes.summary: One-time scaffold of the config the engineering skills assume: which issue tracker to use, the triage label vocabulary, and the domain doc layout, written to docs/agents/ and summarized in CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md.

nodes.label: Pluggable issue-tracker backend
nodes.summary: Skills say 'publish to the issue tracker' and a per-repo config file resolves that to gh issue create, glab issue create, or a markdown file under .scratch/<feature>/, so the skills stay backend-agnostic.

nodes.label: Five canonical triage roles
nodes.summary: needs-triage, needs-info, ready-for-agent, ready-for-human, wontfix, mapped in a per-repo table to whatever label strings the tracker actually uses so skills apply real labels instead of creating duplicates.

nodes.label: CONTEXT.md + ADR domain layer
nodes.summary: A glossary of the project's ubiquitous language plus dated architectural decision records, single-context at the root or multi-context via CONTEXT-MAP.md. Read before exploring; created lazily, never flagged as missing.

nodes.label: Speak the project's domain vocabulary
nodes.summary: Issue titles, refactor proposals, hypotheses, and test names use the glossary's terms and do not drift to synonyms it avoids. A missing term is a signal: either invented language or a real gap to record.

nodes.label: Surface conflicts instead of silently overriding
nodes.summary: Output that contradicts an ADR says so; a plan that contradicts the review rubric goes to the human batched up front; a finding the plan mandates is reported rather than dismissed.

nodes.label: qa: conversational bug reporting into issues
nodes.summary: An interactive session where the user describes problems, the agent lightly clarifies, explores the codebase in a background subagent for context, decides single-issue vs breakdown, and files GitHub issues.

nodes.label: Write issues that survive refactors
nodes.summary: Issue bodies describe user-facing behavior with mandatory reproduction steps and no file paths or line numbers, because those go stale. Prefer many thin, independently fixable issues over few thick ones.

nodes.label: Background exploration subagent
nodes.summary: Kick off a read-only Explore subagent while the conversation continues, to gather domain context without spending the main session's context or blocking the user.

nodes.label: gws-calendar: calendars and events
nodes.summary: Manage Google Calendar v3 — calendars, calendarList, events (insert, list, move, quickAdd, watch), ACLs, freebusy, and settings — plus +insert and +agenda helper commands.

nodes.label: gws-classroom: classes, rosters, coursework
nodes.summary: Manage Google Classroom v1 — courses and their coursework, announcements, topics, students and teachers, plus invitations, registrations, and user profiles with guardians.

nodes.label: gws-chat: spaces and messages
nodes.summary: Manage Google Chat v1 — spaces (create, setup, search, find direct messages), members, messages, space events, media upload/download, and custom emojis, with a +send helper.

nodes.label: gws-docs: read and write Google Docs
nodes.summary: Google Docs v1 — create a blank document, get its latest version, and apply batchUpdate request sets that validate atomically, with a +write helper for appending text.

nodes.label: gws-sheets +append: append rows
nodes.summary: Append one row via --values or bulk rows via --json-values to a spreadsheet by ID. Flagged as a write command requiring user confirmation before execution.

nodes.label: gws-workflow +weekly-digest
nodes.summary: A read-only cross-service rollup combining this week's calendar agenda with the Gmail unread/triage count, output as json, table, yaml, or csv.

nodes.label: Confirm before write commands
nodes.summary: Commands with side effects are flagged as writes and require user confirmation before execution; read-only commands (calendar agenda) are explicitly marked safe.

nodes.label: Session continuity across context resets
nodes.summary: Carrying work across a /clear or a model switch: one side writes a handoff document, the other finds and reads the newest one and briefs from it without re-explaining.

nodes.label: codex handoff: compact a conversation
nodes.summary: Summarize the current conversation into a handoff doc in the OS temp directory, including a suggested-skills section, referencing existing artifacts by path instead of duplicating them, with secrets redacted.

nodes.label: resume: pick up the newest handoff
nodes.summary: Find the newest file by mtime across handoffs/ and, inside the LSATU repo, docs/agent/handoffs/ and docs/implementation-plans/, read it, cross-check the vault ledgers, then emit a four-line briefing and stop.

nodes.label: Brief, then wait
nodes.summary: The orientation skill ends by emitting the briefing and waiting for the human; it does not begin work off the back of what it just read.

nodes.label: Redact secrets before writing an export
nodes.summary: Handoff and export documents strip API keys, passwords, and personally identifiable information before being written out.

nodes.label: second-brain-query: answer from the wiki
nodes.summary: Answer questions against the knowledge base by starting at wiki/index.md, optionally searching with qmd on large wikis, following wikilinks, and citing every claim, with raw sources only as a last resort.

nodes.label: File valuable answers back as pages
nodes.summary: When a query produces a comparison, analysis, or new connection worth keeping, offer to save it into wiki/synthesis/, index it, and log it, so explorations compound instead of evaporating.

nodes.label: Index-first retrieval
nodes.summary: Read the index to identify candidate pages before reading pages, read enough to answer thoroughly but never the whole corpus, and escalate to search tooling only past roughly 100 pages.

nodes.label: extract-design: pull a site's design language
nodes.summary: Run designlang against a URL to extract colors, typography, spacing, shadows, components, breakpoints, and animations, with WCAG scoring, optional dark mode, multi-page crawl, and site-to-site diffing.

nodes.label: Multi-format design token bundle
nodes.summary: Eight files from one extraction: AI-optimized markdown, an HTML preview, W3C design tokens, a Tailwind config, CSS variables, Figma variables, a React theme object, and a shadcn/ui theme.

nodes.label: lovable-prompt: paste-ready Lovable instruction
nodes.summary: Produce a short fenced prompt for Lovable's chat, with a plain-text line on why it must go through Lovable and what to verify afterward. Restates any product constraint the change could violate.

nodes.label: Exhaust the direct path before delegating
nodes.summary: Check whether the task is reachable directly first: schema changes go through Supabase MCP, code changes through the repo, and only genuinely UI-gated platform config falls back to a Lovable prompt.

nodes.label: Terse, no-em-dash house voice
nodes.summary: Joshua's standing style rules recur across skills: no em dashes, no padding with context the target does not need, short prompts in fenced code blocks, one task per prompt.

nodes.label: notebooklm: programmatic NotebookLM
nodes.summary: Full API access to Google NotebookLM including features absent from the web UI: create notebooks, add URL/YouTube/PDF/audio/video/image sources, chat with content, generate every artifact type, and download in multiple formats.

nodes.label: openai-docs: authoritative OpenAI guidance
nodes.summary: Answer OpenAI product, API, and Codex questions from the developers.openai.com MCP server with citations, owning model selection, API model migration, and prompt-upgrade guidance, with browsing restricted to official domains.

nodes.label: higgsfield-soul-id: train an identity model
nodes.summary: Train a Soul Character on a person's face, returning a reusable reference_id that later Higgsfield generations consume via --soul-id. One-time, paid-plan gated, with silent polling.

nodes.label: Restrict answers to authoritative sources
nodes.summary: Prefer the vendor's own docs tooling, verify the API shape against the spec, and confine any fallback browsing to official domains rather than answering from memory or open web content.

nodes.label: Preserve the user's explicitly named target
nodes.summary: When the user names a specific target (a model version to migrate to, a scoped change), keep it even if newer guidance exists; mention the alternative only as optional. Mirrors 'preserve the user's actual intent' in prompt refinement.

nodes.label: Inert skill catalog (activate-by-copy)
nodes.summary: The master skill DB at ~/ai-os/skills/ never auto-loads. A skill runs only once copied (not symlinked, since 2026-07-17) into a project's .claude/skills/ or .agents/skills/. Copies do not follow DB edits, so drift must be re-checked.

nodes.label: Claude/Codex subtree split, never merged
nodes.summary: Skills are filed under claude/ or codex/ by tool origin and are never merged even when byte-identical. A skill that exists for both tools gets one entry under each so each tool's set stays independently editable.

nodes.label: Save-to-both on skill creation
nodes.summary: Creating a skill writes unconditionally to both the current project's .claude/skills/ (or .agents/skills/) and the master DB, project-scoped by default and never auto-promoted to global.

nodes.label: Vendor skills: live symlink + frozen snapshot
nodes.summary: A vendor or plugin skill gets a live symlink under claude/<name>/ reflecting the installed version plus a frozen copy under _snapshots/ for point-in-time reference. Snapshots refresh manually, never on a schedule.

nodes.label: Generated one-line skill index
nodes.summary: skills/INDEX.md is machine-generated by system/scripts/gen-skill-index.py, one line per skill grouped by source type across the claude/ and codex/ splits. Hand-editing is forbidden.

nodes.label: Project forks of catalog skills
nodes.summary: 23 Claude and 28 Codex skills exist as divergent project-local versions (all under the lsatu project) that have drifted from the catalog copy. The index tracks them as a separate 'project fork' class rather than reconciling them.

nodes.label: LLM wiki second brain
nodes.summary: An Obsidian vault where the LLM is librarian: raw sources stay immutable in raw/, the agent compiles them into interlinked wiki pages, and every pass is appended to wiki/log.md. Scaffolded by an interactive 5-step wizard.

nodes.label: Raw sources are immutable
nodes.summary: Files in raw/ are read-only source material and must never be modified. The same read-only-input discipline appears in writing-shape, where the raw material pile is a quarry the skill may never edit.

nodes.label: Index + append-only log ledger
nodes.summary: Every wiki operation updates wiki/index.md (one line per page, under 120 chars) and appends a dated entry to wiki/log.md. Log entries are never edited after the fact; the index is the navigation surface until the wiki outgrows it.

nodes.label: Ingest a source into wiki pages
nodes.summary: Read the source completely, discuss takeaways, write a source summary page, then create or update every entity and concept page it touches, add wikilinks, update the index, and log it. One source may touch 10-15 pages.

nodes.label: Query the wiki, index first
nodes.summary: Answer questions by reading wiki/index.md, then the relevant pages, synthesizing with wikilink citations. Valuable answers are offered back as new synthesis pages so explorations compound. Search the wiki before ever going back to raw.

nodes.label: Wiki lint / health check
nodes.summary: Scan for contradictions between pages, stale claims superseded by newer sources, orphan pages with no inbound links, and missing cross-references. Run after every 10 ingests, monthly at minimum, and before any major synthesis.

nodes.label: Second-brain onboarding wizard
nodes.summary: A five-step one-question-at-a-time wizard (vault name, location, domain, agent configs, optional CLI tools) that scaffolds a new Obsidian vault, generates per-agent config files, installs tooling, and logs the setup.

nodes.label: One schema, many agent configs
nodes.summary: wiki-schema.md is the single source of truth; the Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Gemini config templates are byte-identical apart from output filename and location, each injecting {{WIKI_SCHEMA}} from the same file.

nodes.label: Per-runtime agent config file
nodes.summary: Each runtime reads its own root instruction file: CLAUDE.md for Claude Code, AGENTS.md for Codex, .cursor/rules/second-brain.mdc for Cursor, GEMINI.md for Gemini CLI. Auto-detect the running agent, then offer configs for the others.

nodes.label: Optional local CLI augmentation
nodes.summary: Three optional npm-installed CLIs extend vault work: summarize for link/file/media extraction, qmd for on-device hybrid BM25/vector search once the wiki passes ~100 pages, agent-browser for web research when built-in fetch fails.

nodes.label: Obsidian Web Clipper intake
nodes.summary: The required browser extension that saves web articles as clean markdown straight into the vault's raw/ directory. This is the primary way source material enters the vault without manual copy-paste.

nodes.label: Context window is precious
nodes.summary: Every line of a persistent instruction file must earn its place. Conciseness is scored explicitly, verbose explanations and generic best practices are rejected, and dense beats verbose.

nodes.label: CLAUDE.md audit and improve
nodes.summary: Discover every CLAUDE.md variant in a repo, score each against a six-criterion 100-point rubric, emit a quality report before touching anything, then apply approved targeted diffs.

nodes.label: Scored rubric before intervention
nodes.summary: Assess against weighted numeric criteria and publish the scoreboard before proposing changes. CLAUDE.md scoring runs six criteria to 100 with letter grades; the same report-then-fix ordering is treated as mandatory.

nodes.label: Documentation staleness / drift
nodes.summary: Instruction files rot: commands that no longer run, references to deleted files, outdated tech versions, uncustomized template copy-paste, duplicate info across multiple files. Currency is scored and cross-checked against the real codebase.

nodes.label: Instruction-file templates by project type
nodes.summary: Reusable CLAUDE.md skeletons for minimal root, comprehensive root, package/module, and monorepo root, plus section templates for commands, architecture, key files, style, environment, testing, gotchas, and workflow.

nodes.label: Challenge the plan against the glossary
nodes.summary: Call out immediately when a spoken term conflicts with CONTEXT.md, propose precise canonical terms for fuzzy ones, stress-test domain relationships with invented edge-case scenarios, and surface contradictions between what the user says and what the code does.

nodes.label: CONTEXT.md as glossary only
nodes.summary: CONTEXT.md is a domain glossary and nothing else: no implementation notes, roadmap, architecture decisions, API details, or scratch-pad thinking. Terms are added only after being resolved with the user, updated inline rather than batched.

nodes.label: ADR three-part necessity test
nodes.summary: Offer an ADR only when all three hold: hard to reverse, surprising without context, and the result of a real trade-off with credible rejected alternatives. If any is missing, skip it. ADRs are numbered, factual, and never used for reversible detail.

nodes.label: Create docs lazily
nodes.summary: Create CONTEXT.md only when the first term resolves, and docs/adr/ only when the first ADR is needed. A CONTEXT-MAP.md at the root signals a multi-context repo with per-context glossaries and ADR folders.

nodes.label: Bounded loop with MAX_ROUNDS
nodes.summary: The review loop always terminates at MAX_ROUNDS (default 5). Hitting the cap without approval is reported as an honest deadlock with unresolved points and Claude's counter-position, never as faked convergence.

nodes.label: Read-only sandbox enforcement every round
nodes.summary: Codex runs -s read-only on round 1, but resume rejects -s, so rounds 2+ must force -c sandbox_mode="read-only" or Codex inherits config.toml (possibly danger-full-access) and could write files. Flagged as a critical safety line.

nodes.label: codex exec stdin hang under non-TTY drivers
nodes.summary: codex exec reads stdin in addition to the prompt argument, so under a non-interactive driver it blocks forever at ~0% CPU. The < /dev/null redirect is mandatory on both the fresh and resume calls; a 10-minute timeout ceiling makes any remaining stall fail loud.

nodes.label: Same-session resume preserves critic context
nodes.summary: Round 1 captures thread_id from the thread.started JSON line; every later round resumes that same thread so the critic keeps its prior findings in context rather than re-reviewing cold.

nodes.label: Append-only review log as deliverable
nodes.summary: PLAN-REVIEW-LOG.md records each round's critique plus Claude's response documenting what changed, what was rejected, and why. The log, not the plan alone, is named the deliverable of the process.

nodes.label: PLAN.md locked plan
nodes.summary: The frozen plan written in the project's canonical terms, with goal, numbered approach, key decisions and tradeoffs with ADR links, risks and open questions, and explicit out-of-scope bounds.

nodes.label: Decompose into tiniest working commits
nodes.summary: Break an implementation into the smallest possible commits, each leaving the codebase in a working state, per Fowler's advice to always be able to see the program working. Plans are written in plain English without file paths or snippets, which go stale.

nodes.label: Refactor plan filed as a GitHub issue
nodes.summary: A templated issue with problem statement, solution, commit-by-commit plan, decision document, testing decisions, and out-of-scope bounds, produced after an interview and a test-coverage check of the affected area.

nodes.label: Explicit out-of-scope declaration
nodes.summary: Every plan-shaped artifact ends by naming what it will not do. Appears as the Out of Scope section in the locked plan, the refactor issue template, and writing-shape's own boundary list.

nodes.label: Image-first design-to-code workflow
nodes.summary: For visually important web work the model must generate the design reference images itself, deeply analyze them as a specification, then implement. Freeform coding first is forbidden; the image is the design source and the code is the translation layer.

nodes.label: One section, one large image
nodes.summary: Inside Codex, generate one large image per requested section rather than compressing many sections into one board, so text, spacing, buttons, and typography stay analyzable. Never crop a section out of an older larger render; regenerate it fresh.

nodes.label: Forensic design extraction from reference
nodes.summary: Treat the reference as a spec and extract exact text, type scale relationships, spacing and gutters, button shape and hierarchy, palette, radius logic, grid, and repeated motifs before writing any code. Vague vibe-only analysis is rejected.

nodes.label: Design drift during implementation
nodes.summary: The named common failure: strong references become a generic coded result. Guarded by refusing to simplify into default templates, compress generous spacing, flatten typography, or reintroduce removed nesting. The goal is faithful-to, not inspired-by.

nodes.label: Reject generic AI/SaaS aesthetics
nodes.summary: A rule shared across every UI skill here: no Inter/Roboto defaults, no purple-gradient-on-white, no heavy drop shadows, no gamification or vanity metrics, no AI copywriting cliches. Commit to a specific, intentional aesthetic instead of the model's default.

nodes.label: Combinatorial variance engine
nodes.summary: Before coding, silently roll a coherent combination from enumerated archetypes (vibe/texture, layout, typography, hero architecture, signature components, motion cues) and commit to it, so no two outputs share a layout while all stay premium.

nodes.label: Anti-nested-box vs deliberate double-bezel
nodes.summary: A genuine tension between the two visual skills: image-to-code bans cards-inside-cards and giant rounded wrappers, while high-end-visual-design mandates a deliberate two-layer 'Double-Bezel' outer shell plus inner core with concentric radii for every premium container.

nodes.label: Macro-whitespace and breathing room
nodes.summary: Both visual skills demand doubled section padding (py-24 to py-40), restrained first viewports, and negative space as a design material. Density slop, cramped sections, and overfilled heroes are treated as failures.

nodes.label: Physics-based motion choreography
nodes.summary: All motion simulates mass and spring physics via custom cubic-beziers, never linear or ease-in-out. Covers hamburger morph, staggered mask reveals, magnetic button hover with nested icon translation, and heavy scroll fade-ups.

nodes.label: GPU performance guardrails
nodes.summary: Animate only transform and opacity, never top/left/width/height. backdrop-blur only on fixed or sticky elements, noise overlays only on fixed pointer-events-none pseudo-elements, IntersectionObserver instead of scroll listeners, disciplined z-index layers.

nodes.label: Mobile collapse of asymmetric layouts
