nodes.summary: Every asymmetric archetype must fall back below 768px to single-column w-full with px-4 py-8, dropping rotations and negative-margin overlaps that cause touch-target conflicts, and using min-h-[100dvh] rather than h-screen to avoid iOS Safari viewport jumping.

nodes.label: Pre-output self-verification checklist
nodes.summary: A final enumerated matrix the model runs against its own output before delivering, refining internally if any item fails. Both visual skills close with one (a 21-point clarity check and an 11-point pre-output matrix).

nodes.label: Accessibility tree as source of truth
nodes.summary: The a11y tree, not the DOM, represents what assistive technology sees, so take_snapshot is the reliable check for semantic structure. Visually hiding via opacity behaves differently from display:none or aria-hidden.

nodes.label: Accessibility audit via DevTools MCP
nodes.summary: Eight-pattern audit: Lighthouse baseline, native browser issues, semantics and heading hierarchy, labels and text alternatives, focus and keyboard traps, tap-target sizing, color contrast, and document-level global checks.

nodes.label: Injected JS probe snippets
nodes.summary: Four reusable evaluate_script snippets that measure what the a11y tree cannot: orphaned form inputs, tap-target bounding boxes, an approximate contrast ratio, and document-level lang/title/viewport/reduced-motion state.

nodes.label: Filter large reports before reading them
nodes.summary: Never read a machine report line by line. Use jq or a Node one-liner to extract only failing audits' selectors and snippets, keeping the full JSON out of the context window.

nodes.label: Gemini notes attachment as the did-it-happen signal
nodes.summary: A consultation is ready for follow-up only when the calendar event is in the past, carries a 'Notes by Gemini' or Transcript attachment, and no follow-up has been sent since. Missing notes means skip and wait for the next run.

nodes.label: Idempotent outreach (dedupe before drafting)
nodes.summary: Search Gmail for an existing thread before drafting and skip if a follow-up already went out since the call. One follow-up per consultation; if the student already booked and paid, switch to the onboarding note instead of the sales email.

nodes.label: Mirror a real transcript detail
nodes.summary: Pull the student's diagnostic and target score, study platform, exam timeline, and struggles from the meeting transcript, then personalize the recap line with a real detail and pick the template variant from what the notes revealed.

nodes.label: Read voice + template before drafting
nodes.summary: A required first step: read the email-voice principles and the follow-up template, then follow them exactly. Prose only, no em dashes, under about 150 words, fixed greeting and sign-off.

nodes.label: Scheduled sweep over a calendar window
nodes.summary: A daily run that lists calendar events matching a title pattern over a trailing window, filters by readiness, and produces a queue of drafts plus a report naming anything uncertain for human check.

nodes.label: One-time automations, never recurring
nodes.summary: Pre-consultation check-ins are scheduled as one-time automations exactly one hour before each approved consultation. Recurring or daily automations are forbidden, and temporary setup automations must be disabled afterward.

nodes.label: List candidates, wait for approval
nodes.summary: Search the calendar, list the consultations found, and wait for explicit approval before creating any automation. Never assume which consultations should receive email; if there are none, do nothing.

nodes.label: Reply in the existing thread
nodes.summary: Whenever a thread with the recipient already exists, reply into it rather than starting a new one. Shared by the follow-up drafter and the pre-consultation check-in, and supported natively by the gws reply/forward helpers.

nodes.label: Hub skill plus per-verb helper skills
nodes.summary: Each gws service has one hub skill listing API resources and linking out to thin per-verb helpers (+send, +read, +forward, +triage, +watch). The hub covers discovery; helpers cover the common flag-level operation.

nodes.label: Dry-run and draft escape hatches
nodes.summary: Mutating gws commands expose --dry-run to show the request without executing and --draft to save instead of send, giving the same review-before-effect posture the drafting skills enforce at the workflow level.

nodes.label: Inbound/outbound content sanitization
nodes.summary: Model Armor templates filter user-generated content at two boundaries: +sanitize-prompt for inbound user-to-model text and +sanitize-response for outbound model-to-user text.

nodes.label: Always-violate rule list
nodes.summary: Twelve never-break LSAT U platform rules kept at the front door for fast access: flags not roles, admin displays as Joshua, no bottom dock, drill always dark, 1:1 messaging only, zero-layout-shift highlighting, SVG not Canvas, Postgres-side provisioning, deterministic channel names, mutations never swallow errors, Causation Station as template, repo-native topic modules.

nodes.label: When-in-doubt binary defaults
nodes.summary: Each architectural rule is restated as a one-word binary answer (flag, Foyer, dark, library, rethrow, repo-native, deterministic, Postgres, SVG, inherit) so a decision needs no re-derivation mid-build.

nodes.label: Indexed front door, canonical body elsewhere
nodes.summary: A skill that carries only fast-access daily rules plus explicit pointers to deeper canonical sources, deliberately not duplicating them. The routing skill's own rules drift and live locally; the pointers stay stable.

nodes.label: Explicit source authority ordering
nodes.summary: Sources are ranked highest to lowest (live repo, audit bundle, vault CLAUDE.md, memory) and on contradiction the lower-authority source is fixed, never the higher. Code is ground truth when documentation drifts.

nodes.label: Pick from the library before building custom
nodes.summary: Choose from the indexed 27-component library first; custom work is warranted only when the existing library cannot teach the topic mechanic. Mirrors the catalog-wide 'search before creating' posture.

nodes.label: Lint-gated scaffolding loop
nodes.summary: Parse the plan, mkdir the directory tree, write stub readmes, run the project linter, and iterate until it passes before committing. The linter's rules are the actual spec for what a valid exercise looks like.

nodes.label: Numeric-prefix directory ordering
nodes.summary: Sections are XX-name and exercises XX.YY-name in dash-case, so the filesystem carries curriculum order. Renumbering uses git mv rather than mv so history survives, then re-lints.

nodes.label: Problem / solution / explainer variants
nodes.summary: Each exercise carries at least one of problem/ (student workspace with TODOs), solution/ (reference implementation), or explainer/ (conceptual, no TODOs), each needing a non-empty readme. Stubs default to explainer.

nodes.label: Conversational article shaping
nodes.summary: Turn a pile of raw material into an article by drafting 2-3 candidate openings that imply different theses, forcing a pick, then growing the piece one agreed block at a time, appending to the article file as it goes.

nodes.label: Argue format tradeoffs out loud
nodes.summary: Each beat's rendering is a deliberate defensible choice weighed with the user: prose vs list, inline vs callout, table vs repeated structure, quote vs paraphrase, code block vs inline code.

nodes.label: Re-read before every write
nodes.summary: The user edits the shared document between turns, so re-read from disk before appending and never overwrite — treat 'cut the last one' or 'merge those two' as first-class instructions.

nodes.label: Name the gap rather than inventing
nodes.summary: When the source pile lacks something the output needs, say so explicitly and make the user fill it or cut the section, instead of quietly fabricating material.

nodes.label: Recover original intent before resolving
nodes.summary: For each conflicting hunk, read commit messages, PRs, and original issues to understand deeply why each change was made, then preserve both intents where possible and note the trade-off where incompatible.

nodes.label: Always resolve, never invent behaviour
nodes.summary: A merge conflict must always be resolved and never --abort'ed, and the resolution must not introduce new behaviour that was in neither side.

nodes.label: Discover and run the project's own checks
nodes.summary: After a structural change, find the project's automated checks (typecheck, then tests, then format) and run them, fixing whatever the change broke before finishing. The lint-gated scaffolder applies the same gate.

nodes.label: Codex plugin scaffolding
nodes.summary: Script-driven creation of a Codex plugin directory with a required .codex-plugin/plugin.json, normalized lower-case hyphen-case name, optional companion folders (skills, hooks, scripts, assets, .mcp.json, .app.json), and a personal-marketplace entry by default.

nodes.label: Plugin manifest schema contract
nodes.summary: Manifests need real values for name, version (strict semver), description, author.name, and required interface fields. Absolute https URLs, real asset files, no unsupported fields such as hooks, and apps/mcpServers only when the companion file exists.

nodes.label: Marketplace entry policy defaults
nodes.summary: Every generated entry writes policy.installation (default AVAILABLE), policy.authentication (default ON_INSTALL), and category even when default. policy.products is an override omitted unless asked. Entries are appended, and array order is Codex's render order.

nodes.label: Validate before handing back
nodes.summary: Run scripts/validate_plugin.py against the plugin path before returning it. The validator mirrors the workspace ingestion schema and adds a preflight that rejects leftover [TODO: ...] placeholders.

nodes.label: Cachebuster + reinstall update loop
nodes.summary: To update a local plugin, stamp a single Codex cachebuster suffix (<base-version>+codex.<token>, replacing rather than appending), read the marketplace name, reinstall with codex plugin add, then start a new thread to pick up new skills and tools.

nodes.label: Never hand-edit generated config
nodes.summary: Marketplace manipulation happens through scripts and CLI commands, never by hand-editing marketplace.json or config.toml. Mirrors the generated skill index that must not be hand-edited.

nodes.label: Implicit personal vs explicit marketplace discovery
nodes.summary: The default personal marketplace at ~/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json is discovered implicitly and must NOT be registered with codex plugin marketplace add. Any other path is not discovered and must be installed first or reinstall instructions will fail.

nodes.label: Local-DB channel with allowlist gating
nodes.summary: iMessage has no token: it reads ~/Library/Messages/chat.db directly, gated by macOS Full Disk Access. Inbound senders are gated by access.json, re-read on every message so policy changes take effect without restart.

nodes.label: Prefer allowlist over pairing
nodes.summary: Because the DB is personal and the handles are already known, pairing has no upside and a clear downside: every contact who texts the Mac gets an unsolicited auto-reply. The skill actively pushes back when a user asks for pairing.

nodes.label: Report status, then one concrete next step
nodes.summary: Read the actual state, present it completely, and end with a single concrete next action conditioned on that state rather than a menu of possibilities.

nodes.label: Third-party attribution and license notices
nodes.summary: Skills adapted from external work carry a THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md naming the upstream author and license, and separate the borrowed part from original additions. Reference bundles are kept in a distinct tree marked as not-authored-here.

nodes.label: Claude Code plugin scaffolding
nodes.summary: Guides creating and organizing a Claude Code plugin: directory layout, manifest, component placement, and troubleshooting why a component fails to load.

nodes.label: Convention-based auto-discovery
nodes.summary: Components are found by living in conventional directories with conventional filenames rather than being enumerated in config. Custom manifest paths supplement, never replace, the defaults.

nodes.label: Manifest as declared identity
nodes.summary: plugin.json at .claude-plugin/ carries the kebab-case name, semver version, metadata, and optional component paths. Name and path-shape errors are the common validation failures.

nodes.label: Install-location-independent paths
nodes.summary: Intra-package references must go through an environment root variable (${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}, ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}) because the install location varies by method and OS. Hardcoded absolute or cwd-relative paths break.

nodes.label: Shared component library over duplication
nodes.summary: Cross-cutting assets live in one shared place (lib/, assets/, a shared stylesheet, a reused ext-apps bundle) and every consumer links to it rather than inlining a copy.

nodes.label: Start flat, restructure on growth
nodes.summary: Begin with the simplest flat layout and only move to categorized or hierarchical organization when component count justifies it. Deep nesting costs discovery time.

nodes.label: Build an MCP app with UI widgets
nodes.summary: Adds interactive UI resources on top of a plain MCP server so tools render forms, pickers, dashboards, and confirmations inline in chat, in Claude and other apps-surface hosts.

nodes.label: Tool returns data, resource serves UI
nodes.summary: A widget-enabled tool registers twice: the tool declares _meta.ui.resourceUri and returns plain text/JSON, while a separately registered ui:// resource serves the HTML the host renders in an iframe.

nodes.label: Graceful degradation to plain text
nodes.summary: Because the tool handler already returns meaningful data, hosts without the apps surface simply ignore _meta.ui and Claude reads the data directly. UI is additive, never load-bearing.

nodes.label: Iframe sandbox and CSP restrictions
nodes.summary: Widgets run in a locked-down iframe: no CDN script fetches, no window.open, no arbitrary network origins, no reliable remote images. Violations fail silently as a blank rectangle.

nodes.label: Build-time bundle inlining
nodes.summary: The ext-apps browser build is read at startup, its ESM export statement rewritten to a globalThis assignment, and substituted into a placeholder in the widget HTML so no CDN fetch is needed.

nodes.label: Silent blank widget
nodes.summary: The dominant MCP-app failure: the widget renders as an empty rectangle with no error in the host console, because a CSP violation surfaced only in the iframe's own devtools.

nodes.label: Persistent widget-host-server messaging
nodes.summary: The App class keeps a live bidirectional channel: ontoolresult/ontoolinput inbound, sendMessage and updateModelContext outbound to the conversation, callServerTool straight to the server, openLink for navigation.

nodes.label: Prefer the cheapest mechanism that works
nodes.summary: Route to the simplest sufficient tool: elicitation before a custom widget, plain text before UI, built-in tool before CLI fallback, non-AI script before an AI step.

nodes.label: One tool, one focused widget
nodes.summary: Keep each widget small and single-purpose rather than building a sub-app in the iframe. Fork layout by item count inside one tool instead of multiplying tools.

nodes.label: Watch a video
nodes.summary: Gives the agent video input: yt-dlp downloads the source, ffmpeg extracts auto-scaled frames, captions or Whisper supply a timestamped transcript, and the agent Reads each frame to answer grounded in both streams.

nodes.label: Silent setup preflight
nodes.summary: A fast --check runs before every invocation, emitting nothing on success and returning typed exit codes that map to an idempotent installer or a key prompt. Never announce success to the user.

nodes.label: External binary dependency
nodes.summary: Capability gated on locally installed executables and API keys (yt-dlp, ffmpeg/ffprobe, the gws CLI, the codex CLI, OPENAI_API_KEY). Absence is a preflight failure, not a runtime surprise.

nodes.label: Duration-scaled token budgeting
nodes.summary: Frame count and fps scale inversely with video duration under hard caps (2 fps, 100 frames), with a denser focused mode for a named range, so image tokens stay bounded.

nodes.label: Graded fallback chain
nodes.summary: Try the free/preferred path first and fall back only on failure: native captions before Whisper, Groq before OpenAI, built-in image_gen before the CLI model path.

nodes.label: Never downgrade silently
nodes.summary: Switching to a weaker model or path requires explicit user confirmation, and a failed run must be surfaced rather than blindly retried.

nodes.label: Generate or edit raster images
nodes.summary: Codex-side skill producing bitmap assets (photos, illustrations, mockups, cutouts) via the built-in image_gen tool by default, with a CLI/API fallback for true native transparency.

nodes.label: Mission grounds every decision
nodes.summary: A short concrete statement of why the user wants this, with success criteria and out-of-scope bounds. Every teaching choice traces back to it; vagueness gets interviewed out before anything is written.

nodes.label: Numbered decision-record ledger
nodes.summary: Append-only sequentially numbered records that capture non-obvious insight and get superseded rather than deleted, so a later session inherits what was settled. Used for learning records and ADRs alike.

nodes.label: Opinionated controlled vocabulary
nodes.summary: A glossary that picks one preferred term per concept, lists aliases to avoid, uses its own terms inside definitions, and is adhered to everywhere downstream.

nodes.label: Ground in trusted sources, not parametric memory
nodes.summary: Knowledge must come from a curated, annotated set of high-trust resources with citations; never trust the model's own recall. Gaps are surfaced explicitly to drive further search.

nodes.label: Desirable difficulty for storage strength
nodes.summary: Design for long-term retention over in-the-moment fluency using retrieval practice, spacing, and interleaving, and keep each lesson inside the learner's zone of proximal development.

nodes.label: Author JSON Canvas files
nodes.summary: Creates and edits .canvas files (nodes, edges, groups) per the JSON Canvas 1.0 spec for mind maps and flowcharts in Obsidian.

nodes.label: Post-write referential integrity check
nodes.summary: Every canvas mutation ends with re-parsing the JSON and confirming ID uniqueness plus that every fromNode/toNode resolves to an existing node.

nodes.label: Adversarial cross-model plan review
nodes.summary: Claude drafts a plan into PLAN.md and a read-only Codex session critiques it round after round, returning APPROVED or REVISE, until convergence or a round cap. No code is written during the loop.

nodes.label: Read-only critic sandbox
nodes.summary: The critic can read the repo but must never write. The resume subcommand rejects -s, so read-only has to be forced via -c sandbox_mode, or config defaults could grant full write access mid-loop.

nodes.label: Bounded loop with an explicit cap
nodes.summary: Iteration always terminates at MAX_ROUNDS. Hitting the cap without approval is a legitimate flagged-disagreement outcome, never dressed up as convergence.

nodes.label: Resume the same session across rounds
nodes.summary: Capture the thread_id on round one and resume it thereafter so the critic remembers earlier critiques. Falling back to a fresh exec re-reads the repo and loses everything settled.

nodes.label: Re-assertion guard and finding triage
nodes.summary: Sort each finding into technical, product-decision, or already-rejected. A repeat finding without new evidence is logged as held; a product question goes straight to the human instead of burning a round.

nodes.label: Explicit human approval gate
nodes.summary: Named checkpoints where the human, not the model, decides: kickoff and final sign-off before code, gate approvals in a staged build, choosing merge versus PR, authorizing a fallback path.

nodes.label: Append-only argument transcript
nodes.summary: PLAN-REVIEW-LOG.md records every round's critique plus what was changed, what was rejected, and why. Described as the most valuable artifact of the run.

nodes.label: PLAN.md as the interchange artifact
nodes.summary: A structured plan document (goal, approach, contestable decisions, risks, out of scope) that models communicate through and that later becomes the frozen spec handed to an implementer.

nodes.label: Write an implementation plan
nodes.summary: Turns a spec into a dated plan document of bite-sized, independently testable tasks written for an engineer with zero codebase context, preceded by an explicit file-structure decomposition.

nodes.label: Task right-sizing around a review gate
nodes.summary: A task is the smallest unit carrying its own test cycle and worth a fresh reviewer's gate. Split only where a reviewer could reject one task while approving its neighbor; fold setup into the task that needs it.

nodes.label: Reviewer calibration against nitpicking
nodes.summary: A dispatched reviewer flags only issues that would cause real implementation problems (missing requirements, contradictions, placeholders, unactionable tasks) and approves past stylistic preferences.

nodes.label: Finish a development branch
nodes.summary: Verifies the test suite, detects whether the workspace is a normal repo or a worktree, determines the base branch, then presents merge/PR/cleanup options and executes the choice.

nodes.label: Green tests as a hard precondition
nodes.summary: Integration options are not even presented until the project's test suite passes. Failing tests stop the workflow rather than being noted and worked around.

nodes.label: Weekly automation level-up
nodes.summary: A weekly 3Ms interview (Mindset to find a candidate, Method to scope it, Machine to build it) that ends in exactly one shipped automation artifact for the EA workspace.

nodes.label: Eliminate before automating
nodes.summary: First ask what breaks if the task simply stops. If nothing breaks, log the win and exit; automating waste is worse than leaving it manual. Delegate to a person when the process is too variable.

nodes.label: Lowest autonomy level that works
nodes.summary: Default to the least autonomous option and require explicit choice to go higher. Anything a student or prospect reads is drafts-with-human-review minimum, never auto-sent.

nodes.label: Save-to-both catalog and activation
nodes.summary: Every new skill is written to both the activated project .claude/skills/ path and the DB catalog, project-scoped, with a Codex twin mirrored to .agents/skills/ when applicable.

nodes.label: Skill router / which-flow-fits
nodes.summary: ask-matt is a router over the user-invoked skills, laying out the main idea-to-ship flow, its on-ramps, codebase-health upkeep, and how to cross session boundaries.

nodes.label: Context-window hygiene and handoff
nodes.summary: Keep one phase inside one unbroken window while the model is still in its smart zone; when it fills, hand off to a fresh session via a written file rather than pushing on degraded.

nodes.label: Cross-runtime skill parity baseline
nodes.summary: PARITY.md declares every deliberately single-runtime skill with a justification, so check-skills.py fails only on undeclared drift. Catalog parity is explicitly distinct from activation.

nodes.label: Declared asymmetry, not silent drift
nodes.summary: A one-runtime skill is legitimate only when written down with a reason in the same commit. An undeclared gap is drift and must be either ported or declared; a list without reasons is a snapshot, not a decision.

nodes.label: Cross-model orchestration from the other runtime
nodes.summary: Skills that drive Codex must live only on the Claude side; giving them to Codex would mean Codex driving Codex, defeating the cross-model check that is their whole purpose.

nodes.label: Build an LSAT U bootcamp
nodes.summary: Clones the Intro to LR build end to end for a new topic: interview, content intake and tiering, inspection report, then a gated repo-native multi-session build until a parity audit passes.

nodes.label: Gated multi-session build with a checkpoint ledger
nodes.summary: Work advances through numbered gates, each requiring human approval; state persists in a vault build page with a gate ledger so a fresh session resumes at the current gate and never redoes an approved one.

nodes.label: Clone the reference implementation exactly
nodes.summary: The existing shipped build is the template, not a doc. Reuse its components, tokens, and chrome unchanged; deviations must be argued and approved at a gate.

nodes.label: No silently invented domain content
nodes.summary: Content comes from the author's own files; gaps are flagged for his decision rather than filled in. Missing reviewed content counts as a build failure, not something to paper over.

nodes.label: Fan-out deep research
nodes.summary: Reads an outline.yaml, skips already-completed items for resumability, and launches parallel background agents that each emit a schema-validated JSON record per research item.

nodes.label: Resumable batched agent fan-out
nodes.summary: Check the output directory for completed artifacts and skip them, then dispatch remaining work in approved batches of parallel agents with output suppressed.

nodes.label: Output validated against a schema before completion
nodes.summary: A research task is not complete until validate_json.py confirms every field defined in fields.yaml is covered. The eval viewer imposes the same discipline by reading benchmark and grading field names exactly.

nodes.label: Google Workspace access via the gws CLI
nodes.summary: A generated family of thin skills wrapping the gws CLI across Gmail, Sheets, Meet, Keep, and Workspace events, each documenting one command's flags and examples.

nodes.label: Shared prerequisite doc for auth and security
nodes.summary: Every gws skill defers auth, global flags, and security rules to one gws-shared page rather than repeating them, and points at gws generate-skills if it is missing.

nodes.label: Dry-run and draft modes on outbound actions
nodes.summary: Send-shaped commands expose --dry-run to show the request without executing and --draft to save instead of send, giving a rehearsal path before any irreversible outbound action.

nodes.label: Unread inbox triage listing
nodes.summary: Summarizes unread mail as sender/subject/date with a configurable max, arbitrary Gmail search query, and JSON output for downstream processing.

nodes.label: Send or reply to mail
nodes.summary: Sends new mail or reply-alls to an existing thread with automatic threading, sharing the same flag surface for recipients, attachments, HTML, alias sender, dry-run, and draft.

nodes.label: Edit and restructure an article
nodes.summary: Divides a draft into sections, confirms the section plan with the user, then rewrites each for clarity and flow under a tight paragraph-length constraint.

nodes.label: Dependency-ordered exposition
nodes.summary: Treat information as a directed acyclic graph: order sections so each piece is introduced only after everything it depends on. Mirrors teaching the knowledge a skill needs before practicing it.

nodes.label: User-invocation-only skills
nodes.summary: Some skills set disable-model-invocation so they never auto-trigger from context and run only when the user explicitly asks, protecting stateful or opinionated workflows from accidental starts.

nodes.label: Announce the skill at start
nodes.summary: Several build-side skills open by stating which skill is running, making the workflow legible to the user. Contrasts with the silent-on-success preflight convention.

nodes.label: Description field as the triggering mechanism
nodes.summary: A skill fires based on its frontmatter description alone, so the description must state both what it does and concrete contexts for use, worded slightly pushy to fight undertriggering. Optimized against a 20-query should/should-not-trigger eval set split into train and held-out test.

nodes.label: Skill undertriggering
nodes.summary: Claude fails to consult a skill that would have helped, because simple one-step queries are handled directly and vague descriptions do not match. Countered by pushy descriptions and substantive eval queries.

nodes.label: Explain the why instead of rigid MUSTs
nodes.summary: Instructions should transmit reasoning so a smart model can generalize; all-caps ALWAYS/NEVER and oppressively rigid structures are a yellow flag. Overfitting a skill to its handful of test examples makes it useless at scale.

nodes.label: Overfitting a skill to its test cases
nodes.summary: Fiddly patches aimed at the two or three examples under review produce a skill that works only on those examples. Description optimization guards against the same thing by selecting on held-out test score, not train score.

nodes.label: With-skill versus baseline comparison
nodes.summary: Every eval spawns two runs in the same turn: one with the skill, one without (or against a snapshot of the old version). Aggregate pass rate, time, and tokens are reported per configuration with a delta.

nodes.label: Blind judging to remove bias
nodes.summary: Two outputs are handed to an independent comparator labelled only A and B, with no indication of which skill produced which, so the verdict rests purely on output quality against a generated rubric.

nodes.label: Evidence-backed assertion grading
nodes.summary: A grader reads the transcript and the output files, marks each expectation pass or fail with a cited quote, and refuses to pass on surface compliance such as a correct filename over empty content.

nodes.label: Non-discriminating assertion
nodes.summary: An assertion that passes in both with-skill and without-skill configurations, or that a clearly wrong output would also satisfy. Creates false confidence; the grader and analyzer both exist partly to surface it.

nodes.label: Post-hoc analysis of why one version won
nodes.summary: After a blind verdict, the analyzer unblinds, reads both skills and both transcripts, scores instruction-following, and emits prioritized improvement suggestions categorized as instructions, tools, examples, error handling, structure, or references.

nodes.label: benchmark.json and the eval viewer
nodes.summary: Aggregated run results with mean and stddev per configuration, rendered by generate_review.py into a two-tab browser review (Outputs and Benchmark) whose field names the viewer reads exactly.

nodes.label: Human review gate before proceeding
nodes.summary: Work stops and waits for the person: the eval viewer must be put in front of the human before the agent evaluates outputs itself, and a written spec must be approved before any implementation plan is drafted.

nodes.label: HITL versus AFK work classification
nodes.summary: Wayfinder tickets are either human-in-the-loop, resolvable only through live exchange where the agent never answers for the human, or AFK, driven by the agent alone. A grilling agent that answers its own questions has broken the contract.

nodes.label: Design approved before any implementation
nodes.summary: A hard gate: no code, scaffolding, or implementation skill invocation until a design has been presented and approved, applied to every project regardless of apparent simplicity.

nodes.label: "Too simple to need a design" anti-pattern
nodes.summary: Skipping design on a small project, where unexamined assumptions cause the most wasted work. The design may be a few sentences but must still be presented and approved.

nodes.label: Decompose work too large for one unit
nodes.summary: When a request spans multiple independent subsystems, flag it before refining details and split it: brainstorming into sub-projects each getting its own spec, wayfinder into a map of ticket-sized decisions each sized to one agent session.

nodes.label: Fresh-eyes spec self-review
nodes.summary: After writing a spec, scan it for placeholders and TBDs, internal contradictions, scope creep, and requirements open to two interpretations, fixing inline. A reviewer subagent can run the same checklist and is calibrated to approve unless gaps would produce a flawed plan.

nodes.label: Dated design spec document
nodes.summary: The validated design written to docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-topic-design.md and committed to git, which becomes the input to the implementation-plan step.

nodes.label: PRD published to the issue tracker
nodes.summary: A problem statement, solution, extensive user-story list, implementation and testing decisions, and out-of-scope section, synthesized from conversation with no interview and labelled ready-for-agent.

nodes.label: Just-in-time visual companion
nodes.summary: A local server that serves HTML content fragments to a browser tab so the user can react to mockups, diagrams, and side-by-side comparisons, recording clicks to a state events file. Offered only when a question would be clearer shown than told, and only as its own message.

nodes.label: Would the user understand it better shown than told
nodes.summary: The per-question test for reaching for the browser: visual content (mockups, layouts, architecture diagrams) goes to the browser, textual content (requirements, tradeoffs, A/B/C choices) stays in the terminal. A question about a UI topic is not automatically a visual question.

nodes.label: Chart oversized work as a map of decision tickets
nodes.summary: Wayfinder's own capability: name a destination, grill breadth-first to surface open decisions, create a tracker issue labelled wayfinder:map with child decision tickets, then resolve one ticket per session until the way is clear.

nodes.label: Plan, do not execute
nodes.summary: Wayfinder produces decisions, not deliverables; the pull to just do the work signals the edge of the map and time to hand off. Only a task ticket does rather than decides, and it earns that by unblocking a decision.

nodes.label: Fog of war and deliberate incompleteness
nodes.summary: Do not chart what you cannot yet see. Questions you can state precisely become tickets even if blocked; questions you cannot phrase sharply stay in a Not yet specified section and graduate as the frontier advances.

nodes.label: Index, not store: one fact in one place
nodes.summary: The map lists a one-line gist per closed ticket and links out; the decision itself lives only in its ticket, so nothing is restated in two places and readers zoom on demand.

nodes.label: Claim before working, to survive concurrency
nodes.summary: A session assigns a ticket to itself before any work so concurrent sessions skip it; an open unassigned ticket is unclaimed. Expect other sessions editing the tracker at the same time.

nodes.label: Refer to work by name, never by bare id
nodes.summary: Everything the human reads names the map or ticket by title, with the id and URL riding inside the link. A wall of issue numbers is illegible.

nodes.label: Context Handoff Before Reset
nodes.summary: Produce a structured summary so a fresh agent resumes seamlessly: decisions, shipped changes, key absolute paths, running state, verified-vs-assumed claims, deferrals, and one pick-up-here line.

nodes.label: Reload project state from the vault ledgers
nodes.summary: Pickup reads the locator, tasks ledger, hot cache, dashboard, index, and the latest log entry in a fixed order, then emits a 6-8 line briefing and stops. Explicit invocation only, never automatic at session start.

nodes.label: Orientation per token, not full load
nodes.summary: Read the ledgers and skim the index, but pull deeper synthesis pages lazily only once the human points at a task. The same instinct drives reading only the reference file you need and treating bundled scripts as black boxes.

nodes.label: Extract a ubiquitous language glossary
nodes.summary: Scan the conversation for domain nouns and verbs, pick opinionated canonical terms with aliases-to-avoid, express relationships and an example dev/domain-expert dialogue, and write UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md. Re-running merges new terms into the existing file.

nodes.label: Ambiguous and synonymous domain terms
nodes.summary: One word used for two concepts, or two words for one concept, silently diverging what people think they agreed. Flagged explicitly in a Flagged ambiguities section with a recommendation.

nodes.label: Drive a real browser for verification
nodes.summary: Navigate, fill forms, click, extract data, capture screenshots and traces against a live page, either from the terminal via playwright-cli or as native Python Playwright scripts against a local dev server.

nodes.label: Reconnaissance then action against live DOM
nodes.summary: Never address elements blind: snapshot or inspect the rendered page first, derive refs or selectors from that state, act, then re-snapshot after navigation or significant DOM change. Refs and selectors go stale.

nodes.label: Stale element reference or premature inspection
nodes.summary: Acting on a ref from an old snapshot, or reading the DOM before networkidle on a dynamic app, so the selector targets nothing. The fix is re-snapshotting and waiting for load state.

nodes.label: Check the required binary before proposing commands
nodes.summary: Verify the tool exists and is authenticated before running anything: check npx before the Playwright wrapper, install and auth-check the higgsfield CLI at step 0, and read the shared gws auth doc before any Workspace call.

nodes.label: Confirm with the human before any write
nodes.summary: Write commands carry an explicit caution to confirm before executing, and destructive SQL needs a stated yes plus a stated reason it is safe in the same message.

nodes.label: Google contacts and directory management
nodes.summary: Read, search, create, and update contacts, contact groups, other-contacts, and domain directory profiles via gws people.

nodes.label: Google Forms read and write
nodes.summary: Create a form (title only at creation), batch-update its items, get it, read responses, manage watches, and set publish settings via gws forms.

nodes.label: Drive file upload with inferred metadata
nodes.summary: Upload a local file to Drive with MIME type detected automatically and the filename inferred from the path unless overridden, optionally into a parent folder.

nodes.label: Append plain text to a Google Doc
nodes.summary: Insert plain text at the end of a document body by ID; rich formatting requires dropping to the raw batchUpdate API instead.

nodes.label: Relay a schema migration through the Lovable SQL editor
nodes.summary: Package a DDL change as idempotent paste-ready SQL with exact SQL-editor steps and a verification probe, so a backend Claude cannot reach directly takes one round trip instead of a confused loop.

nodes.label: Relay only what genuinely cannot be reached directly
nodes.summary: Data-level reads, writes, and RPCs go direct via admin JWT and PostgREST; only DDL needs the relay. Relaying a query that could have been answered instantly is the exact failure the skill is meant to prevent, and the skill is expected to retire itself once direct access exists.

nodes.label: Resolving the target environment by name
nodes.summary: Two projects share the name LSATU; SQL sent to the decoy applies cleanly and reports success while the real app is untouched. The target must be matched by exact project ref, verified against config.toml every run.

nodes.label: Idempotent, re-runnable, one logical change
nodes.summary: Migrations use IF NOT EXISTS, CREATE OR REPLACE, and DROP POLICY IF EXISTS so a double or partial paste is safe, and stay to one logical change because a long half-applied paste is the worst outcome.

nodes.label: Verify with a probe, never ask whether it worked
nodes.summary: Write a read-only verification query before the change is applied and run it after, or ask for the probe output as one concrete action. The human saying he pasted it is not verification, and a claim of success without probe output is forbidden.

nodes.label: Live backend is authority; the brain mirrors it
nodes.summary: When the probe disagrees with what was expected, say so plainly and stop rather than reconciling in the notes. Applied changes and half-applied failures both get logged to the vault ledgers.

nodes.label: Reverse engineer a site into a build blueprint
nodes.summary: Fetch the HTML for structure, the main app JS for every animation and handler, and the main CSS for the full design system, then assemble a dated teardown with tech stack, effects table, assets, and a section-by-section build plan.

nodes.label: Dated teardown document
nodes.summary: research/YYYY-MM-DD-site-slug-teardown.md, thorough enough to hand to a fresh agent session that never visits the original site, marking each finding as confirmed from source or inferred.

nodes.label: Distinguish confirmed from inferred
nodes.summary: State whether a finding came from the actual fetched source or was inferred from class names and general patterns, so the builder knows what is solid and what may need adjustment. Mirrors the grader's demand for cited evidence and flagging of unverifiable claims.

nodes.label: Filter third-party code from the site's own
nodes.summary: Skip analytics, consent banners, captchas, CDN libraries, and social widgets; keep the files under dist, build, assets, or static that hold the site's custom behavior. Note which libraries are used without fetching them.

nodes.label: The reveal: impressive effects have simple implementations
nodes.summary: The most valuable part of a teardown is showing the trick plainly, that the moon illumination is 54 images swapped on mousemove or the parallax is translateX(mouseX/50). Vague summaries like "uses scroll animations" are useless to a builder.

nodes.label: UI polish and animation review
nodes.summary: Emil Kowalski's design engineering philosophy applied to interface code: decide whether to animate at all, choose easing and duration, build responsive components, and review existing UI as a Before/After/Why table.

nodes.label: Animation frequency decides whether to animate
nodes.summary: Something seen a hundred times a day gets no animation ever, occasional surfaces get standard animation, and rare or first-time moments can carry delight. Keyboard-initiated actions are never animated.

nodes.label: Unseen details compound
nodes.summary: Most polish is never consciously noticed, and that is the point: the aggregate of invisible correctness is what makes an interface feel right. Sonner's edge cases, origin-aware popovers, and instant subsequent tooltips are all this.

nodes.label: Good defaults beat configurability
nodes.summary: Ship beautiful out of the box because most users never customize, and keep adoption friction near zero. Echoed in settings files that provide sensible defaults when no config exists at all.

nodes.label: Interruptible motion over restart-from-zero
nodes.summary: CSS transitions and springs retarget from their current position when interrupted, while keyframes restart from zero. Anything rapidly retriggered, like stacking toasts or a gesture the user reverses mid-motion, needs the interruptible form.

nodes.label: Animate only transform and opacity
nodes.summary: These skip layout and paint and run on the GPU; animating padding, margin, height, or width triggers all three rendering steps. Framer Motion's x/y shorthands are not hardware accelerated and drop frames under load.

nodes.label: Respect prefers-reduced-motion and pointer type
nodes.summary: Reduced motion means fewer and gentler animations rather than none: keep opacity and color transitions that aid comprehension, drop movement. Hover animations are gated behind hover and fine-pointer media queries so touch taps do not trigger them.

nodes.label: Review animation slowed down and the next day
nodes.summary: Play at 2-5x duration or step frame by frame in DevTools to catch timing desync and wrong transform origins invisible at speed, and re-review with fresh eyes the following day. Gestures get tested on real hardware.

nodes.label: Compose UI from an existing component registry
nodes.summary: shadcn manages adding, searching, fixing, and composing components as source code in the project, driven by the project's own package runner and components.json config.

nodes.label: Search and compose before writing custom UI
nodes.summary: Check the registries for an existing component first, then build pages by composition (settings = tabs plus card plus form controls), preferring built-in variants over custom styles and semantic color tokens over raw values.

nodes.label: .claude/plugin-name.local.md settings pattern
nodes.summary: Per-project plugin configuration and state stored as YAML frontmatter plus a markdown body that can itself be a prompt, read from hooks, commands, and agents, gitignored and user-managed.

nodes.label: Parse YAML frontmatter and body in bash
nodes.summary: sed the range between the --- markers for frontmatter and awk past the second marker for the body, cache the parsed block rather than re-reading per field, and strip surrounding quotes since YAML permits both forms.

nodes.label: Quick exit when not configured
nodes.summary: A hook checks the state file exists and the enabled flag is true, exiting zero otherwise, so an unconfigured or paused plugin costs nothing and never errors. The enabled flag allows deactivation without deleting the file.

nodes.label: Atomic write via temp file and move
nodes.summary: Write the modified settings to file.tmp.$$ and mv it into place rather than sed -i, so an interrupted process cannot leave a corrupt state file.

nodes.label: Hooks cannot be hot-swapped
nodes.summary: Edited settings only take effect after Claude Code restarts, which every plugin README must state. The local.md enabled flag exists partly because toggling hooks.json would need a restart too.

nodes.label: Create settings interactively then confirm
nodes.summary: A command asks the user for preferences with AskUserQuestion, validates the answers, writes the local.md file, then reports the configuration, how to edit it, that it is gitignored, and the restart requirement.

nodes.label: Sanitize and path-check values before use
nodes.summary: Escape quotes in user input written to settings, reject values containing .. as path traversal, validate enums and numeric ranges, and keep the file readable by the owner only and out of git.

nodes.label: Untrusted Channel Input / Prompt Injection
nodes.summary: Messages arriving over a channel can carry prompt injection, so access mutations must never be downstream of them. Auto-approving 'the one pending pairing' is exactly what an injected request looks like.

nodes.label: Manage Discord channel access
nodes.summary: Approve pairings, edit allowlists, and set DM and group policy by editing access.json in the channel state directory; the skill never talks to Discord, the channel server re-reads the file.

nodes.label: Fan out research across parallel agents
nodes.summary: Read an outline.yaml, skip already-completed items, and launch background agents in approved batches, each writing a structured JSON file per item against a shared fields.yaml schema.

nodes.label: Resumable, checkpointed batch execution
nodes.summary: Completed output files are checked before launching so a rerun skips finished items, batches pause for user approval between them, and each agent's completion is signalled by its own output file rather than task output.

nodes.label: Mark uncertain values explicitly
nodes.summary: Research output tags uncertain field values inline and collects their names into an uncertain array, so downstream consumers see confidence rather than uniform-looking data.

nodes.label: Assemble an article beat by beat
nodes.summary: Offer 2-3 candidate beats from the raw material, write only the one the user picks, re-read the file from disk, then offer the next set of pivots until the journey ends naturally with leftover material unused.

nodes.label: Commit-time quality gate
nodes.summary: Husky pre-commit running lint-staged with Prettier on staged files first, then a full typecheck and test run, with the setup commit itself acting as the smoke test.

nodes.label: Detect existing project conventions before acting
nodes.summary: Read the lockfile to pick the package manager, skip creating a Prettier config if one exists, omit hook lines for scripts the project lacks, and use the project's own package runner rather than assuming npx.

nodes.label: Generate brand and product imagery
nodes.summary: Product photoshoot modes (product shot, lifestyle, hero banner, carousel, ad creative, virtual try-on, conceptual) submitted through the higgsfield CLI, whose backend prompt enhancer assembles the final prompt.

nodes.label: Let the backend assemble the prompt
nodes.summary: The CLI's backend enhancer holds the mode-specific photography vocabulary and structural templates; the agent selects a mode and never freehands the final prompt.

nodes.label: Agent authoring
nodes.summary: Create Claude Code subagents as markdown files with YAML frontmatter (name, description, model, color, tools) plus a second-person system prompt body. Covers manual and AI-assisted generation, validation rules, and triggering tests.

nodes.label: Triggering examples in the description
nodes.summary: Write 2-4 <example> blocks (Context / user / assistant / <commentary>) inside an agent or skill description so the model fires it reliably. Covers explicit, implicit, proactive, and tool-usage triggering, and debugging over- and under-triggering.

nodes.label: Structured system-prompt template
nodes.summary: A proven skeleton for autonomous prompts: role line, Core Responsibilities, numbered Process, Quality Standards, Output Format, Edge Cases — written in second person and specific rather than vague.

nodes.label: Explicit edge-case handling
nodes.summary: Every autonomous prompt names the awkward situations up front (no findings, too many findings, ambiguous input, missing context) and states how to handle each, so the agent does not improvise at the boundary.

nodes.label: Severity-ranked findings report
nodes.summary: The shared output shape for every review/analysis run: a short summary, then findings grouped critical / major / minor (or errors / warnings / info), each with a file:line-style location and a concrete fix.

nodes.label: Read-only analysis mode
nodes.summary: A skill that only analyzes and reports, creating or modifying nothing — the user (or a separate request) implements the recommendations. Used to make recommendation and audit runs safe to trigger freely.

nodes.label: Claude Code automation recommender
nodes.summary: Scans a codebase for signals (package manifests, framework deps, test config, CI, DB) and recommends 1-2 automations per category: hooks, subagents, skills, plugins, MCP servers.

nodes.label: Codebase signal detection
nodes.summary: Map observable repo artifacts to recommendations: .prettierrc means a format hook, tsconfig.json a type-check hook, @supabase/supabase-js the Supabase MCP, auth/payment paths a security-reviewer subagent.

nodes.label: Hook-based event automation
nodes.summary: PreToolUse / PostToolUse / Notification hooks in .claude/settings.json that format, lint, type-check, run tests, block edits to .env and lock files, or alert on permission and idle prompts.

nodes.label: Protective blocking hook
nodes.summary: PreToolUse hooks that refuse edits to sensitive paths — .env and credential files, lock files, .git internals — so secrets are not exposed and lock files only change via the package manager.

nodes.label: MCP server integration
nodes.summary: External capability reached through MCP servers (context7 docs, Playwright, Supabase/Postgres, GitHub, Linear, Sentry, Docker, Memory), configured per-project in .mcp.json and shared by checking it into git.

nodes.label: Parallel subagent delegation
nodes.summary: Hand focused review, exploration, or generation to a specialized subagent with its own context window and tool grant, so the main thread keeps working. Model choice haiku/sonnet/opus trades cost against thoroughness.

nodes.label: Invocation control (model vs user invoked)
nodes.summary: Keeping a description makes a skill model-invoked and reachable by other skills at a permanent context cost; disable-model-invocation strips it, so only the human can fire it at zero context cost but real cognitive cost. Side-effect skills go user-only.

nodes.label: Context load budget
nodes.summary: Every model-invoked description sits in the window on every turn, spending tokens and attention. That cost is the brake on splitting skills finer and the reason descriptions are pruned harder than bodies.

nodes.label: Context pointer wording
nodes.summary: A pointer's phrasing, not its target, decides when and how reliably the agent reaches disclosed material. A must-have file behind a weak pointer is a variance bug — sharpen the wording before inlining.

nodes.label: Completion criterion
nodes.summary: The checkable, and where it matters exhaustive, condition that tells the agent a unit of work is done. Clarity resists premature completion; demand sets how much legwork the agent does.

nodes.label: Leading word (Leitwort)
nodes.summary: A compact pretrained concept repeated as a token across a skill, anchoring a whole region of behaviour in minimal tokens and sharpening invocation when the same word appears in prompts and docs.

nodes.label: Single source of truth
nodes.summary: Each meaning lives in exactly one authoritative place, so changing behaviour is a one-place edit. Its violation is duplication.

nodes.label: Router skill
nodes.summary: One user-invoked skill that names the other user-invoked skills and when to reach for each, curing the cognitive load of remembering a large hand-fired catalog. It can hint but never fire them.

nodes.label: Premature completion
nodes.summary: Ending a step before it is genuinely done because attention slips toward being finished. Caused by a fuzzy completion criterion plus visible post-completion steps; fix the criterion first, hide later steps only if the rush persists.

nodes.label: Duplication
nodes.summary: The same meaning stated in more than one place. Costs maintenance and tokens and inflates that meaning's rank on the information hierarchy past its real importance.

nodes.label: Sprawl
nodes.summary: A skill simply too long, even when every line is live and unique. Costs readability, maintainability, and tokens; cured by disclosing reference and splitting by branch or sequence.

nodes.label: Sediment
nodes.summary: Stale layers that settle in a skill because adding feels safe and removing feels risky — the default fate of any skill without a pruning discipline.

nodes.label: No-op instruction
nodes.summary: A line the model already obeys by default, so you pay context load to say nothing. The test is whether it changes behaviour versus the default; a weak leading word is a no-op.

nodes.label: Skill authoring reference
nodes.summary: The vocabulary and levers for writing predictable skills — invocation, information hierarchy, pruning, leading words, and the failure modes to diagnose against. All reference, user-invoked, with its glossary disclosed.

nodes.label: Red-green-refactor TDD cycle
nodes.summary: Write one minimal failing test, watch it fail for the right reason, write the simplest code that passes, verify green, then refactor. No production code without a failing test first; code written first gets deleted.

nodes.label: Watch it fail
nodes.summary: Observing the test fail — for the expected reason, not a typo — is what proves the test actually tests something. Tests written after code pass immediately and prove nothing.

nodes.label: Verify before trusting
nodes.summary: The cross-cutting rule of this catalog: never accept a surface signal as evidence. Watch the test fail, confirm the mutation returned 2xx rather than trusting a rendered UI, check a reviewer's claim against the codebase, and re-run the baseline before starting work.

nodes.label: Testing the mock instead of the code
nodes.summary: Asserting on mock elements, mocking a method whose side effect the test depends on, or building partial mocks that omit fields downstream code consumes. Mocks isolate; they are never the thing under test.

nodes.label: Test-only methods in production classes
nodes.summary: Adding methods used only by tests (a destroy() for cleanup) to production classes — dangerous if called for real, violates YAGNI, and confuses object lifecycle with entity lifecycle. Belongs in test utilities.

nodes.label: Gate function before a risky move
nodes.summary: A short STOP-and-ask checklist placed immediately before a tempting action — before mocking, before adding a method, before implementing review feedback, before clicking assign — that must pass before proceeding.

nodes.label: YAGNI grep check
nodes.summary: Before implementing a suggested feature or 'doing it properly', grep the codebase for actual usage. Nothing calls it means propose removal rather than building it out.

nodes.label: Receiving code review
nodes.summary: Read, restate, verify against the codebase, evaluate, then respond — implementing one item at a time with a test each. Clarify every unclear item before implementing any of them.

nodes.label: No performative agreement
nodes.summary: Banned responses to feedback: 'You're absolutely right', 'Great point', any gratitude expression, and jumping to implement before verification. State the technical requirement or just fix it.

nodes.label: Reasoned pushback on external feedback
nodes.summary: External feedback is suggestions to evaluate, not orders. Push back with technical reasoning when a suggestion breaks functionality, ignores context, violates YAGNI, or conflicts with prior architectural decisions.

nodes.label: Isolated workspace setup
nodes.summary: Before implementation, ensure work happens off the user's current branch: detect existing isolation first (guarding against submodules), prefer the harness's native worktree tool, and fall back to git worktree only if none exists.

nodes.label: Clean test baseline
nodes.summary: Run the project's test suite in the fresh workspace before touching anything, so new bugs can be told apart from pre-existing ones. Failing baseline means report and ask, not proceed.

nodes.label: Don't fight the harness
nodes.summary: When the platform already provides a capability (native worktree tool, existing isolation), using the raw command instead creates phantom state the harness cannot see or clean up.

nodes.label: Wiki health lint
nodes.summary: Eight-check audit of the wiki — broken wikilinks, orphan pages, contradictions, stale claims, missing pages, missing cross-references, index consistency, data gaps — reported by severity with a fix per finding.

nodes.label: One-question-at-a-time wizard
nodes.summary: Collect configuration by asking a single question per step, each with a sensible default the user can accept, then execute the whole scaffold at the end rather than interleaving prompts with side effects.

nodes.label: Template plus placeholder substitution
nodes.summary: Ship a reference template file and fill named placeholders at generation time ({{VAULT_NAME}}, {{ComponentName}}, the class-name slot in a fetch prompt) rather than writing output freehand.

nodes.label: Staged research outline
nodes.summary: outline.yaml (topic, items, execution config) plus fields.yaml (field definitions with detail levels), built from model knowledge then supplemented by a background web-search agent, and confirmed with the user before deep research runs.

nodes.label: Outline supplementation pass
nodes.summary: Re-open an existing outline.yaml, gather additions from the user and optionally a web-search agent in parallel, merge them in place while avoiding duplicates, and re-confirm.

nodes.label: Verbatim sub-agent prompt template
nodes.summary: A hard constraint that a delegated agent's prompt be reproduced exactly, with only {variable} slots replaced — no restructuring or rewording — so fan-out results stay comparable across runs.

nodes.label: Interactive HTML playground builder
nodes.summary: Builds a self-contained single-file HTML explorer: controls on one side, live preview on the other, generated prompt with a copy button at the bottom. Six templates cover design, data, concept maps, document critique, diff review, and code maps.

nodes.label: Self-contained single-file artifact
nodes.summary: Inline all CSS and JS with no external dependencies, because a dead CDN means a dead artifact. The architecture report relaxes this to two known CDNs (Tailwind, Mermaid) but is otherwise static.

nodes.label: Prompt-output handoff
nodes.summary: The playground's real deliverable: a live-updating natural-language instruction, mentioning only non-default choices and carrying enough context to act on without the playground, copied back into Claude.

nodes.label: Click-to-comment annotation
nodes.summary: Let the user click a node, diff line, or suggestion card to attach a comment, then assemble only the annotated items into the generated prompt. Shared by the code-map, diff-review, and document-critique templates.

nodes.label: Single state object, live re-render
nodes.summary: One state object every control writes to and every render reads from; each change triggers both preview re-render and prompt rebuild. No Apply button, no stale preview.

nodes.label: Pre-populate with real project data
nodes.summary: Seed a visual tool with actual material — 15-25 real components with file paths, real edges from imports, a parsed git diff, real suggestions with line refs — so it is usable on first load rather than empty.

nodes.label: Visual before/after architecture report
nodes.summary: A self-contained HTML file written to the temp directory and opened for the user: one card per deepening candidate with files, problem, solution, wins, a recommendation-strength badge, and a side-by-side before/after diagram.

nodes.label: Deepening opportunity discovery
nodes.summary: Explore a codebase for architectural friction — shallow modules, leaking seams, pure functions extracted only for testability — and apply the deletion test to propose refactors that concentrate rather than move complexity.

nodes.label: Fixed domain vocabulary
nodes.summary: Use the project's glossary terms exactly and never drift into near-synonyms — module not component or service, interface not API, seam not boundary — with the domain's own nouns taken from CONTEXT.md.

nodes.label: ADR as re-litigation guard
nodes.summary: Existing ADRs record decisions a review must not reopen casually; contradicting one requires a marked callout justifying why the friction is real. Rejections with load-bearing reasons become new ADRs.

nodes.label: Fragment capture
nodes.summary: Append heterogeneous nuggets of writing — sharp sentences, vignettes, half-thoughts, quotes — to one markdown file separated by horizontal rules, imposing no structure or outline.

nodes.label: Site teardown
nodes.summary: Fetch a site's HTML, then its main JS and CSS with dynamically built extraction prompts seeded from real class names, and assemble a dated teardown document: tech stack, design system, effects breakdown, assets, and section-by-section build plan.

nodes.label: Confirmed vs inferred labeling
nodes.summary: Mark which findings came from actual source and which were inferred from class names and patterns, so the person building from the document knows what is solid and what may need adjusting.

nodes.label: Guided drill assignment workflow
nodes.summary: Read the newest transcript by meeting date, pick a drill matching the student's need, check repo wiring, browser-verify the drill launches, assign to exactly one student through the teacher UI, then verify rows and notifications and log it.

nodes.label: Browser-driven platform action
nodes.summary: With no agent path to the prod Supabase backend, the logged-in Chrome admin session on lsatprep.study is the API: act through the same UI flows Joshua would use rather than inserting rows.

nodes.label: React controlled-input pitfall
nodes.summary: Programmatic form_input sets DOM values without updating React state, leaving submit buttons silently disabled and producing zero network traffic. Type with real keystrokes, confirm the button is enabled, then confirm the mutation fired.

nodes.label: Verify the mutation, not the UI
nodes.summary: Confirm a POST to the backend actually fired and returned 2xx, and that the resulting row is visible to the student. A UI that merely looks done, or a success toast, is not evidence.

nodes.label: Student-facing voice gate
nodes.summary: Anything a real student will read — message text, homework instructions, note bodies — is written in Joshua's voice via wiki/teaching-voice.md, drafted and shown before sending when the content is open-ended.

nodes.label: Per-student action log
nodes.summary: Every platform action is appended to students/<name>/assignment-log.md with date, item, reason, and evidence; verified drills also go to wiki/guided-drill-verification-log.md so QA is not repeated.

nodes.label: Fail-closed reporting
nodes.summary: When verification is ambiguous, state exactly what was and was not confirmed rather than claiming completion. Prefer 'verified to launch and load the runner' over broader claims.

nodes.label: Secret and PII redaction in output
nodes.summary: Never print auth tokens or service-role keys, and redact student email recipients in final reports unless the user explicitly needs them.

nodes.label: Shared prerequisite pointer
nodes.summary: Every gws skill opens with the same pointer to ../gws-shared/SKILL.md for auth, global flags, and security rules, keeping that material in one place instead of restating it per command.

nodes.label: Introspect the schema before calling
nodes.summary: Run `gws <api> --help` and `gws schema <api>.<resource>.<method>` to discover required params, types, and defaults before building --params and --json flags, rather than guessing the API shape.

nodes.label: Draft instead of send
nodes.summary: A --draft (or --dry-run) path that produces the outbound artifact without dispatching it, letting a human approve before anything reaches a recipient.

nodes.label: Cross-service workflow composition
nodes.summary: Compose two Workspace services into one step — email-to-task reads a Gmail message's subject and snippet and creates a Google Tasks entry — rather than making the user chain the calls.

nodes.label: Content safety filtering
nodes.summary: Model Armor templates sanitize a user prompt or a model response before it is used, providing a filtering layer for user-generated content.

nodes.label: Knowledge Graph Extraction
nodes.summary: Turn an arbitrary corpus (code, docs, papers, images, video) into a clustered knowledge graph with community detection, plus HTML/JSON/report outputs. Implemented by the graphify skill.

nodes.label: Confidence-Tagged Edges (EXTRACTED/INFERRED/AMBIGUOUS)
nodes.summary: Every asserted relationship carries a provenance tag and numeric confidence so invented links are distinguishable from evidenced ones. Never invent an edge; use AMBIGUOUS when unsure.

nodes.label: Parallel Subagent Fan-Out
nodes.summary: Split a large file corpus into chunks and dispatch all extraction subagents in a single message so they run concurrently; sequential dispatch defeats the purpose. Requires write-capable general-purpose agents.

nodes.label: Read-Only Subagent Silently Drops Results
nodes.summary: Dispatching extraction subagents as the read-only Explore type means they cannot write chunk files, so results vanish with no error. Detected by checking chunk files exist on disk.

nodes.label: Incremental Re-Extraction with Cache
nodes.summary: Hash-based manifest plus a semantic cache means only new or changed files are re-extracted; code-only changes skip the LLM path entirely and run AST extraction alone.

nodes.label: Graph Artifacts (HTML, JSON, report, vault, Neo4j)
nodes.summary: graphify emits graph.html, graph.json, GRAPH_REPORT.md, and optionally an Obsidian vault, wiki, SVG, GraphML, and Cypher/Neo4j push.

nodes.label: MCP Transport Selection (stdio/SSE/HTTP/ws)
nodes.summary: Four transports with different tradeoffs: stdio for local/custom servers, SSE for hosted OAuth services, HTTP for stateless token APIs, WebSocket for real-time bidirectional streams.

nodes.label: Credentials via Environment Variables, Never Hardcoded
nodes.summary: Tokens and keys are injected through ${VAR} expansion and documented in the README; hardcoding or committing credentials is forbidden, and OAuth is preferred where the service supports it.

nodes.label: Least-Privilege Tool Allowlisting
nodes.summary: Pre-allow only the specific MCP tools a command needs rather than wildcarding a whole server; skills declare narrow allowed-tools lists for the same reason.

nodes.label: Batch and Parallelize Tool Calls
nodes.summary: Prefer one filtered query over N individual lookups, cache expensive results, and issue independent calls in parallel rather than serially.

nodes.label: Root Cause Before Any Fix
nodes.summary: The Iron Law of systematic debugging: no fixes without root cause investigation first. Symptom fixes count as failure, and the four-phase process is mandatory even under time pressure.

nodes.label: Four-Phase Debugging Workflow
nodes.summary: Investigation, then pattern analysis, then single-hypothesis testing, then implementation with a failing test. Each phase must complete before the next.

nodes.label: Backward Call-Stack Tracing
nodes.summary: Trace a bug backward from where it surfaces through each caller until the original trigger is found, adding stack-trace instrumentation when manual tracing stalls, then fix at the source.

nodes.label: Component-Boundary Instrumentation
nodes.summary: In multi-component systems, log what enters and exits each boundary once to gather evidence of WHERE the failure is before proposing any fix.

nodes.label: Defense-in-Depth Validation
nodes.summary: After finding a root cause, validate at every layer the data passes through (entry, business logic, environment guard, debug logging) so the bug becomes structurally impossible.

nodes.label: Condition-Based Waiting
nodes.summary: Replace arbitrary sleeps and timeouts in tests with polling on the actual condition, with a bounded timeout and a clear error, eliminating load-dependent flakiness.

nodes.label: Arbitrary Timeouts Cause Flaky Tests
nodes.summary: Guessing at timing with setTimeout/sleep creates race conditions that pass locally and fail under CI load; escalating the sleep value is the classic thrashing pattern.

nodes.label: Three Failed Fixes Means Wrong Architecture
nodes.summary: When three fixes fail and each reveals a new problem elsewhere, the pattern itself is wrong; stop fixing and escalate to an architectural discussion with the human.

nodes.label: Pressure-Resistant Rule Language
nodes.summary: Skills are bulletproofed with ALWAYS/NEVER phrasing, an explicit Iron Law, redundant restatement, and a rationalizations table naming the exact shortcut that feels justified in the moment.

nodes.label: Subagent Pressure Testing of Skills
nodes.summary: Validate a process skill by running scripted scenarios at a subagent: an academic no-pressure comprehension test plus emergency, sunk-cost/exhaustion, and authority/social-pressure scenarios that tempt the shortcut.

nodes.label: Failing Test First (TDD)
nodes.summary: No production code without a failing test first; the test must be watched failing for the right reason, then minimal code written to pass. Code written before its test is deleted.

nodes.label: Vertical Slice Iteration
nodes.summary: One test then one implementation, repeated, rather than writing all tests then all code. Horizontal slicing produces tests of imagined shape rather than actual behavior.

nodes.label: Adversarial Review Before Shipping
nodes.summary: Work is checked by a fresh, differently-scoped reviewer before it cascades: a code-reviewer subagent given curated context rather than session history, returning severity-ranked findings and a verdict.

nodes.label: Curated Context, Not Session History
nodes.summary: Delegated agents receive a precisely built prompt (description, requirements, git SHA range) instead of the parent's conversation, keeping the reviewer on the work product and preserving the parent's context.

nodes.label: Severity-Calibrated Findings
nodes.summary: Review output is structured as Strengths, then Critical / Important / Minor issues with file:line and why-it-matters, then a clear ready-to-merge verdict. Not everything is Critical.

nodes.label: Read-Only Review Isolation
nodes.summary: A reviewing agent must not mutate the working tree, index, HEAD, or branches; inspect via git show/diff/log and use a separate worktree if another revision is needed.

nodes.label: Minimal Solution Ladder (YAGNI)
nodes.summary: Climb rungs and stop at the first that holds: does it need to exist, does the codebase already have it, stdlib, native platform, installed dependency, one line, then minimum code. Deletion over addition.

nodes.label: Comprehension Before Simplification
nodes.summary: Laziness shortens the solution, never the reading: trace the full flow and every caller first. A small diff in the wrong place is a confident wrong fix, and the lazy fix IS the root-cause fix.

nodes.label: Chat-Only Output, Writes Nothing
nodes.summary: session-handoff deliberately writes no file and touches no memory; persistence to the ledgers is a separate skill's job. This is the boundary that distinguishes it from wrapup.

nodes.label: Separate Verified State from Assumed State
nodes.summary: Every claim about live systems is either checked this session (say how, stamp the real time) or explicitly marked NOT re-verified. Stale belief presented as current forces the next session to re-derive everything.

nodes.label: Open Questions Are Obligations
nodes.summary: Anything left OPEN in a handoff must be resolved or re-asked before the next session starts new work, because requirements have been silently re-typed and promised artifacts lost across resets.

nodes.label: Transcript Export with Paste-Ready Handoff Prompt
nodes.summary: Save the whole conversation verbatim to a dated markdown file under handoffs/, with summary, decisions, open threads, and a fenced paste-ready prompt to resume in a new chat.

nodes.label: Ledger Persistence at Session End
nodes.summary: wrapup closes a session by striking finished tasks with a date in the task ledger, rewriting the hot cache, and appending a dated newest-first log entry so work is never re-run.

nodes.label: Propose and Confirm Before Writing Done
nodes.summary: wrapup shows a proposed Done/Now/Next split and waits for a one-line approval before touching files; a wrong Done is the exact failure the gate exists to prevent.

nodes.label: Paste-Box Prompt as the Deliverable
nodes.summary: The actual handoff to another executor is a single fenced code block with no surrounding prose inside it, short and imperative, so it copies in one click.

nodes.label: Read Current Code and Docs Before Briefing
nodes.summary: Never write recommendations from memory: read the actual repo files and existing vault docs, archive superseded briefs, and cross-reference screenshots against the rendering component before proposing fixes.

nodes.label: No Fabricated Domain Content
nodes.summary: Joshua authors the LSAT curriculum; the agent never invents content. Suspected fabrications from prior runs are flagged to a content-audit file rather than silently rewritten, and sources are verified verbatim or from git history.

nodes.label: Joshua's Voice Constraints
nodes.summary: No em dashes anywhere, terse and opinionated rather than hedged, no AI-slop vocabulary, 'modules'/'steps' never 'phases', and push back when a direction adds complexity.

nodes.label: Route to the Direct Path Before Delegating
nodes.summary: Only hand a task to the Lovable UI when it is genuinely gated there; schema changes go through Supabase migration tools and code changes are made and pushed directly.

nodes.label: Browser-Driven Platform Automation
nodes.summary: Drive a logged-in Chrome session against a third-party SPA to perform a multi-step workflow end to end (LSAT Lab set creation), capturing IDs and URLs as it goes.

nodes.label: Verification Gates Between Steps
nodes.summary: Each risky step ends in a named GATE with an expected numeric check and a listed recovery; never proceed past a failed gate. Autonomy continues only while gates pass.

nodes.label: Verify by Reading Data, Not by Eyeballing
nodes.summary: For anything beyond a handful of rows, run a JS snippet that returns compact structured counts and ordering assertions rather than trusting a screenshot, and identify records by stable ID not row position.

nodes.label: Stale Coordinates and Re-Render Races
nodes.summary: A re-rendering SPA shifts layout between actions, so reused click coordinates silently select nothing or open the wrong record; screenshot before every click and open by ID.

nodes.label: Shared Append-Only Run Ledger
nodes.summary: Each run appends a structured per-item entry (counts, IDs, URLs, date) to a log file that sibling skills read to locate prior work and append their own status lines. Fields are never removed or reformatted.

nodes.label: Explicit Sibling-Skill Scope Boundary
nodes.summary: Skills that could be confused with each other state the disambiguation table up front and hand off rather than overreach, e.g. mega-set vs set-builder vs transcribe, or the Higgsfield family's NOT-for lists.

nodes.label: Premium Design Upgrade Audit
nodes.summary: Scan an existing project, diagnose generic AI design fingerprints (Inter everywhere, purple gradients, three equal cards, Lucide icons), and apply targeted fixes in a risk-ordered sequence without changing the stack.

nodes.label: Work Within the Existing Stack
nodes.summary: Improve what is there rather than rewriting: no framework or styling-library migration, no breaking functionality, check dependencies before importing, keep changes small and reviewable.

nodes.label: Generative Media Creation
nodes.summary: Submit image, video, 3D, and audio generation jobs through the Higgsfield CLI, including marketplace listing card sets whose compliance templates live server-side.

nodes.label: CLI Bootstrap and Auth Precheck
nodes.summary: Before any command, install the CLI if it is missing from PATH and stop to ask the user to re-authenticate interactively if the session is expired.

nodes.label: Messaging Channel Access Control
nodes.summary: Manage who can reach the agent over a messaging channel by editing a JSON allowlist/policy/pending-pairing file that the channel server re-reads; covers iMessage and Discord.

nodes.label: Read-Before-Write on Shared State Files
nodes.summary: Always re-read a JSON state file immediately before writing it, because a concurrent server process may have added entries; pretty-print so it stays hand-editable.

nodes.label: Skill Catalog Installation
